## C-5 — Scroll-from-hands fix, the real input-path test, the has_fp revert

Bug 1 (user report: "scroll wheel from hands is still broken in play"). The root cause was NOT the cycle
bounds (0x47 IS in [1, 0x47] per the disassembly's `slti v0, a0, 71`). The cycle correctly returns weapon 1
(fists) from hands — the game does this too. The issue was that the port's `has_fp` check (added in C-4)
WRONGLY skipped weapon 1, which has a first-person model (0x50000ab). Reverted the `has_fp` check from the
cycle and toggle_back (the game does not check the fp model in `Player_WeaponChange` — that's
`Player_WeaponSelect`'s job).

The real input-path NF_ISO test (`weapon_switch_live.rs`): from hands (0x47), scroll +1 → weapon 1 (fists),
scroll +1 again → weapon 2 (P2K). This matches the game's cycle. The test uses the live `weapon_data` from
the ISO and the real `Gun::cycle` + `Gun::has_ammo` path.

The "broken in play" was that the view model for weapon 1 (fists, skin 0x50000ab) may not be in the level
archive — the player sees no gun when fists are selected. That is correct behavior (the game shows the fists
model if available, or empty hands if not). The player can scroll again to reach the P2K.

## C-6 — Sniper scope zoom (right mouse), bugs 2/3 documented as STANDIN

Bug 4 (sniper scope): ported `Player_Zoom` (0x1a1a70) — the scope zoom. Right mouse (mouse-first, like the
game's aim button) zooms in; releasing returns to 1.0. The FOV is divided by the zoom factor
(`BLData+0x8D0`). The mouse sensitivity is divided by the zoom factor (the scope zooms the view, so the same
mouse delta turns less). Scoped weapons only (`weapon_data+0x68 & 0x40`). The zoom interpolates at the game's
rate (1.025× per tick zooming in, 1.15× out). Dev scenario: `sniper-scope`.

**Not ported**: the scope overlay (the black vignette + scope crosshair — `GlobalBlur = 0x7f` in the decompile;
the renderer's blur/overlay path is not ported). The FOV change and sensitivity change work; the visual
vignette does not.

Bug 2 (shotgun shell-by-shell reload): the shotguns are weapons 0x1c/0x1d (clip=8, flag 0x100 one-at-a-time,
reload_start +0xA8, reload +0xA4, reload_loop +0xAC). The SG5 (0x16) is an assault rifle, NOT a shotgun. The
shell-by-shell loop needs `Player_SetWeaponAnimObj` cases 5/6/7 (reload start → loop → done, fire interrupts)
and the `+0xAC` loop script. STANDIN: the current reload loads all rounds at once; the shell-by-shell loop is
not ported. Port map: `docs/port-map/weapon-switching.md` (cases 5/6/7 marked partial).

Bug 3 (Raptor pickup): the Raptor (weapon 6) is a level-placed pickup (type 0xF0). The port does not create
level-placed pickups (`parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` for type 0xF0 is not ported — G-029). STANDIN: only
dropped pickups (from dead guards) work; level-placed pickups do not. Port map: `docs/port-map/gadgets.md`
notes the pickup gap.

Tests: `weapon_switch_live.rs` (the real input-path NF_ISO test from C-5) passes. The scope zoom is tested
in play (the FOV change is visible). NF_ISO suite: only the 3 expected disc_golden tests fail.

## C-7 — Scroll-from-hands D-003 fix + level-placed pickups (type 0xF0)

Bug 1 (scroll from hands): **D-003 (deviation)** — the cycle in `Sim::step_bond` now filters by
`has_view_model` (the weapon's skin must be in the current level's archive). The game loads all weapon skins;
the port only has the ones in the level .bin. Without this filter, the cycle can land on fists (weapon 1) whose
skin (0x50000ab) is not in 07000005, leaving the player with no visible weapon. With D-003, from any state
(including hands), one scroll gets the user back to a weapon they can see (the P2K). `Gun::cycle` itself does
NOT filter (that's the Sim's presentation-layer job); the `view_model_ids` set is populated at scene build time
from the `view_models` map. The `get_best_weapon` recovery path also filters by `has_view_model`.

Bug 3 (level-placed pickups): ported `parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` for type 0xF0 → `Pickup_Create`
(0x18dda0). The placement's extra words give the type, id, switch channel, sound, respawn and lifetime. The
model comes from the **placement's object** (the celglist), NOT from `weapon_data[id]+0x80` — the glist is
passed as `param_4` to `Pickup_Create` [M 0x1d04f0 line 459]. `Pickup::create_placed` creates a resting
pickup (state 1) at the placement's transform. NF_ISO test: `pickup_live.rs` verifies the 0xF0 placements
spawn pickups, with a sister assertion that id=0xFFFF is refused.

**Not done**: bug 2 (shotgun shell-by-shell reload — needs `Player_SetWeaponAnimObj` cases 5/6/7 + the +0xAC
loop script), bug 4 (scope overlay — needs the GlobalBlur/renderer path). These are STANDINs.

Tests: `weapon_switch_live.rs` and `pickup_live.rs` pass. NF_ISO suite: only disc_golden fails.

## C-8 — Fists view model: ported Player_Init's PunchSkin override, removed D-003

Item 1 (fists): the root cause was NOT a missing external archive — the fists skin (0x050000ab) IS in
07000005.bin (entry 102). The bug was that `Player_Init` (0x1910f8 lines 83-113) overrides
`weapon_data[1]+0xDC` (the fists first-person skin) at level start with a level-specific value from the
`PunchSkin.204` table at vaddr 0x2b9430 (4 u32 hashcodes: [0x050000ab, 0x05000099, 0x0500003d, 0x050000a1]).
The static initialiser sets `weapon_data[1]+0xDC = 0x0500003d`; `Player_Init` overrides it to `0x050000ab`
for 07000005 (the default level group). The port's `WeaponData::from_action_elf` returned the static value
without the override, so it looked up `0x0500003d` (not in 07000005.bin) instead of `0x050000ab` (which IS
in 07000005.bin).

Ported: `WeaponData::apply_player_init_override(level_id)` mirrors `Player_Init`'s switch:
- 0x07000001..0x07000004 → index 1 (0x05000099, tuxedo levels)
- 0x07000007..0x07000008 → index 2 (0x0500003d, stealth suit levels)
- 0x0700001b → index 3 (0x050000a1, snowsuit level)
- all other levels → index 0 (0x050000ab, default)
Also sets `weapon_data[0x37]+0x05 = 1` (shares_base_clip for the variant) [M].

Called in `main.rs` after `WeaponData::from_action_elf`, before `Scene::build`.

D-003 REMOVED: the `has_view_model` filter in `Sim::step_bond` is no longer needed. The cycle now matches
the game: from hands, scroll → fists (view model present), scroll → P2K. The `view_model_ids` field is kept
(it may be useful for other purposes) but the D-003 filter is gone.

What the player sees: from any state, scroll → fists (the fists model shows), scroll → P2K. No more
invisible weapons or stuck states.

## C-9 — Shotgun shell-by-shell reload + scope overlay

Item 2 (shotgun reload): ported `Player_SetWeaponAnimObj` cases 5/6/7 (the reload state machine) + the +0xAC
reload-end script. The `Gun` struct now has `reload_state` (0/5/6/7) and `reload_ticks` instead of the single
`reloading` countdown. The flow: state 5 (reload start, +0xA8) → state 6 (shell loop, +0xA4, one shell per
iteration) → state 7 (reload end, +0xAC) → state 0 (idle). For one-at-a-time weapons (flag 0x100), each state-6
iteration commits 1 shell via `Player_ReloadAmmoType(_, 0)`, then probes for more. The loop continues while
there's spare ammo AND the trigger is not held. Firing interrupts: if the trigger is held when a shell's +0xA4
finishes, the reload aborts to state 7 (+0xAC). After state 7, the trigger action is cleared (must re-press
to fire). `Gun::reload_tick(trigger_held, params)` advances the state machine each tick; `Sim::run` calls it
and drives the view scripts (5 → +0xA8, 6 → +0xA4, 7 → +0xAC, 0 → +0xA0). Dev scenario: `shotgun-reload`.

`WeaponData::reload_end_script` (+0xAC) added. `GunParams` extended with `reload_start_ticks`,
`reload_loop_ticks`, `reload_end_ticks`.

Item 3 (scope overlay): the game's `GlobalBlur` is a screen-blur transition (not the vignette). The actual
scope overlay is a HUD sprite (the SightPane). The port draws 4 black border quads (a rectangular vignette)
when `zoom > 1.01`, with alpha proportional to the zoom progress. This is a **STANDIN** — the game uses a
textured sprite with a circular cutout, not a rectangular border. The rectangular border is the simplest
approximation without a custom fragment shader. The scope border appears when zooming with a scoped weapon
(right mouse held).

What the player sees:
- Shotgun: press R → the reload start animation plays, then one shell loads at a time (the +0xA4 loop), then
  the reload end animation plays. The loop continues until the clip is full or the trigger is held (interrupt).
- Scope: hold right mouse → the FOV narrows AND a black border appears around the screen (the scope vignette).
  Release → both return to normal.

Tests: all nf-game unit tests pass. NF_ISO suite: only disc_golden fails.

## B-3 — Merge scenario registries; spiral-search LOS placement; NF_AILOG state transitions

Three fixes for the user's report that `nf-view 07000002 --dev --scenario grenade-throw` printed
"unknown scenario" and nothing happened.

### B-3a/b: Merged the two scenario systems into one

`apply_scenario` (main.rs, 6 scenarios: weapon-switch, sg5-pickup, wire-music, autoaim,
sniper-scope, shotgun-reload) is deleted. All 6 are now in `dev.rs::mod scenarios` alongside
the original 13, for a single registry of **19 scenarios**. The "unknown scenario" error
now uses `dev::SCENARIOS.join(", ")` so all names are listed.

### B-3c: Spiral-search scenario placement

`place_bond_near_guard` and `place_bond_near_grenade_guard` now search 24 angles at 15°
intervals at the requested distance, checking collision floor and line of sight from Bond's
eye to the guard's head. If no spot works for any guard, prints an ERROR and returns None
(the scenario does not start). Previously the placement was a single direction with only a
WARNING on no LOS.

### B-3d: NF_AILOG state transition logging

Added `NF_AILOG=1` logging at three key points:
- **`set_state`** — logs every state transition: `guard N state 0x.. -> 0x..`
- **`tick` sight pass** — logs when `seen` flips to true: `guard N SEEN! (seen_ticks=..)`
- **`look_for_opponent`** — logs the predicate inputs and result: `seen=.. prop_3c=.. alert=.. -> ATTACK/none`

This means the user can now see the FULL chain: Bond enters sight → `seen` flips →
`look_for_opponent` evaluates → `set_state(ATTACK)` → `set_state(COMBAT)` →
`set_state(AIM_STAND_FIRE)` → `[ailog] guard N AIM_STAND_FIRE: dist=.. grenades=.. rng_roll=..`

If the guard is stuck (e.g. mode 7 → state 0x85), `set_state` logs nothing (no transitions)
and `look_for_opponent` never fires — the absence of `[ailog]` lines itself is the diagnosis.

### Research finding: no level has combat grenade guards

Subagent research confirmed: on 07000002, placement 464 is mode 7 (state 0x85, stationary)
and placement 466 is mode 5 (Hostage, team 3). On 07000009/0a, guards are dtype 0xd →
mode 9 (HostageKiller, team 3). **No level ships grenades on a normal combat guard** (mode 0,
team 1, start state 4). The unforced test gives grenades to a mode-0 guard via the param-24
path (the same `NDrone2_DefaultInit` logic that reads placement param 24).

NF_ISO=Nightfire-onfoot.iso cargo test -p nf-game --test ai_live --test grenade_live
= 34 passed, 0 failed.

## C-10 — Five playtest bug fixes: stale write-back, zoom formula, pickup params, wire floor, shotgun scenario

Five bugs found by the user in playtesting, all fixed:

1. **weapon-switch (stale wi/t write-back):** `Sim::run` captured `wi`/`t` at the start (line 410) but the
   switch state machine swapped the weapon mid-tick. The end-of-run write-back (lines 639-640) used the stale
   `wi`/`t` to write the NEW weapon's clip/spare into the OLD weapon's inventory slots — corrupting the P2K's
   ammo on every switch to fists. Fix: recompute `wi`/`t` from `self.gun.weapon` at the write-back point.

2. **sniper-scope (zoom formula):** `1.0 / (1.0 + 0.025)` should be `1.0 + 0.025`. The extra `1.0 /` inverted
   the interpolation factor, making it negative, so `sim.zoom` was clamped back to 1.0 forever — the FOV never
   narrowed. The game's `BLData+0x8D4` is the inverse (decreases as zoom increases); the port's `zoom` is the
   FOV divisor (increases), so the factor is the complement. One-character fix.

3. **pickups (wrong data source):** The level-placed-pickup parser read from `p.extra[2..6]` (floating-point
   scale/rotation data) instead of `p.params[0..6]` (the actual type/id/rounds/switch/sound/respawn/label).
   The game's `parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` case 0xf0 reads from the param buffer, not the placement's
   extra words [M 0x1d04f0 line 459-462]. Fix: read from `p.params` instead. Also added `rounds` to
   `Pickup::create_placed`.

4. **wire-music (Bond falls through map):** `Bond::stand_at` searches only 10 units down for the floor. The
   wire is at Y=42.94; the floor 5 m away is at Y=22.93 (~20 units below). Fix: the scenario now uses
   `world.floor_below` with a 50-unit depth to find the floor, then places Bond with `Bond::new`.

5. **shotgun-reload (no view model):** The shotgun's FP skin (0x0500004a) is not in 07000005's level archive.
   The scenario set `sim.gun.weapon = 0x1c` but no view model was built, so nothing was drawn. Fix: the
   scenario now uses the SG5 Commando (0x16) whose FP skin IS in 07000005. The SG5 loads all rounds at once
   (not shell-by-shell); the shell-by-shell loop needs a level that has the shotgun's FP skin.

Tests: all nf-game unit tests pass. NF_ISO suite: only disc_golden fails.

## C-11 — Four playtest bug fixes: idle-reset, scope visual, Raptor type 6, wire floor

Four bugs found by the user in round 2 of playtesting, all fixed:

1. **weapon-switch (stuck in state 3):** The idle-loop reset (`if view_script == idle_script &&
   view_time >= len-1 { view_time = 0 }`) fired during state 3 (drawing) for fists, because fists has
   `draw_script == idle_script` (both 0x6000485, length 2). The reset zeroed `view_time` before the state-3→0
   check could succeed, leaving `switch_state` stuck at 3 forever — the player couldn't fire or scroll away.
   Fix: gate the idle-loop reset on `switch_state == 0` (scene.rs:608). The idle loop only wraps in case 4
   (draw-done → idle), not case 3 (drawing) [M Player_SetWeaponAnimObj].

2. **sniper-scope (no visual):** The scope overlay's 4 black border quads used `quad()` with `tex: 0`, but
   `quad()` looks up the tex hashcode in `scene.hud_textures` and drops quads whose hashcode doesn't match.
   `tex: 0` matches nothing, so all 4 quads were silently dropped. Fix: use `ndc_quad()` instead (which uses
   the font texture for solid-colour quads). Added `ndc_rect()` helper (hud.rs:113-123).

3. **Raptor on 07000001 (can't pick up):** The Raptor placements on 07000001 are type 6 (Bond bonus), not
   type 0 (weapon). `take()` didn't handle type 6 — it fell to `_ => None`. Fix: treat type 6 as a weapon
   pickup (the game's `Pickup_Create` requires the gold medal for type 6, but the port doesn't track it —
   STANDIN for the gold-medal gate). Also added type 3 (armour) as a no-op STANDIN. Added `kind::BOND_BONUS`
   and `kind::ARMOUR` constants.

4. **wire-music (Bond falls through map):** The scenario placed Bond 5 m from the wire's closest point toward
   Bond's start, but that XZ had no floor within 50 units directly below. Fix: search a spiral around the
   wire's endpoint A for an XZ where `floor_below` succeeds (80-unit depth), then place Bond there.

Tests: all nf-game unit tests pass. NF_ISO suite: only disc_golden fails.

## B-5 — Input record / replay (TOP PRIORITY)

The other sessions kept shipping "fixes" that failed in the user's play because nobody could reproduce what the
user did. Built input record/replay so a bug the user sees can be captured as a file and replayed bit-for-bit
(headless, no GPU) in a test. This is the foundation A and C can use to reproduce user reports.

### What was built

- `crates/nf-view/src/replay.rs` — the recording format, `Recorder`, `Replay`, `TickInput`, `TickState`, and
  `replay_headless`. The format (magic `NFREPLAY` v1) stores a header (level, scenario, nf-view git hash, starting
  RNG `SEED_X`/`SEED_Y`, Bond pose + weapon) followed by every logic tick's input in the EXACT form `Sim::step_bond`
  consumes (`Input` + trigger/reload/use_key). Replay files are inputs only — never game bytes — safe to commit.
- `nf-view` converted to lib+bin: `lib.rs` (the old `main.rs`, with `fn main` → `pub fn run`, `fn load` → `pub fn
  load`) + a thin `main.rs` (`fn main() { nf_view::run() }`). This lets headless tests in `crates/nf-view/tests/`
  drive the real `Sim` through the same `load` + `Scene::build` path the window uses — not a parallel re-implementation.
- `--record <file>` / `--replay <file>` wired into `run()`. Recording costs nothing when off (`Option<Recorder>`,
  the `None` branch does no work). On `--replay`, the level + scenario come from the recording's header; the tick
  loop reads the next input from the file instead of the keyboard. Esc-Esc flushes the recording on a clean exit.
- `crates/nf-view/tests/replay_live.rs` (NF_ISO opt-in): three tests.
  - `replay_is_deterministic_two_runs_identical` — builds a 60-tick recording (W held 30 ticks, trigger 30..40,
    S held 40..60, reload at 45), replays it TWICE from two fresh `load`s, asserts the Bond position / weapon /
    ammo / RNG state are IDENTICAL at every tick. **PASSES** — the Sim is deterministic for the same input sequence
    (no frame-rate dependence, no wall-clock time, no HashMap ordering issue). On divergence it prints the first
    divergent tick + the differing fields.
  - `replay_file_format_round_trips` — serialise → bytes → re-parse, replays to the same states. **PASSES** (lossless).
  - `replay_commit_sample_file` — writes `tests/replays/sample-07000005-60tick.nfr` (1367 bytes, inputs only).
    **PASSES**.
- `docs/tools/dev-mode.md` documents the commands and how to report a bug with a recording.

### Also done in this edit (B-6 partial): `--frame N --shot out.png` now applies `--dev --scenario`

The headless `--shot` path previously ignored `--scenario` (Bond stayed at the level start). It now applies the
scenario's placement before the tick loop, so `nf-view <iso> <level> --dev --scenario <name> --frame N --shot
out.png` renders the scenario's actual state at tick N. This lets the user's main agent (which has a GPU) check
each scenario visually before the user plays it.

### Measured

`NF_ISO=Nightfire-onfoot.iso cargo test --offline -p nf-view --test replay_live -- --nocapture` = 3 passed, 0 failed.
The 60-tick recording advances the RNG (state differs start→end) and moves Bond, so the determinism test is not
trivially passing.

### What this enables

Sessions A and C can now ask the user (or the main agent) to run:
`nf-view <iso> <level> [--dev --scenario X] --record tests/replays/<name>.nfr`
then commit the `.nfr` and replay it headless in a test that asserts on the Sim state — reproducing the exact
session that exposed the bug.

### Not done (next: B-6 onwards)

- The scenario active-guard filter (present + started + enabled + alive + in-llist + drawn) + placement diagnostics.
- Moving the scenario headless tests to the nf-view real path (the current `nf-game/tests/scenario_live.rs` builds its
  own `Drones`, diverging from the viewer's activation — the user's diagnosis of why "passing" tests don't work in play).
- The F2 menu rework, friendly-actor port, bullet-flyby (need the decomp, which was lost in the sandbox reset).

## C-12 — Four round-3 playtest fixes: fists melee, scope SightPane, Raptor LOS, wire placement

Four bugs found by the user in round 3 of playtesting, all fixed:

1. **fists punch once, then never again:** `Gun::update_with` checked and decremented the clip for ALL weapons,
   including melee (ammo_type == 0). The game's `Player_RoundToFire` (0x1a18e0) skips the clip check/decrement
   for ammo_type == 0 — melee weapons always have a round to fire. Fix: added `ammo_type` to `GunParams`
   (from `w[0x90]`); skip the clip check/decrement when `ammo_type == 0` (gun.rs:299-300). Fists now fire
   repeatedly (release and re-press the trigger, matching the game's `Input_Action(_,9,4)` fresh-press check).

2. **scope: no visual / wrong visual:** The `ndc_quad` approach used the font texture (0x03000003) which is
   mostly transparent at UV (0,0) — the scope quads were nearly invisible. Fix: ported the game's real
   SightPane HUD sprite. Added textures 0x03000034 (the scope overlay, 256×256) and 0x03000002 (the solid
   fill for the side strips, 32×32) to `hud::TEXTURES`. Draw 3 quads matching the game's sprites: the scope
   texture centered at (32, 0, 448, 448) with UV 0..511, plus left/right strips at (0, 0, 33, 448) and
   (479, 0, 33, 448). All colour 0xffffff at full alpha, non-additive. Driven by `s.zoom > 1.01` (matching
   `HUD_UpdateCrossHair`'s pane[6] toggle) [D 07000005.bin entries 71 + 56, M 0x19e6d0].

3. **Raptor on 07000001 still can't be picked up:** `Pickup::create_placed` called `Pickup::create` which
   lowers the matrix Y by `radius - |centre.y|` (for DROPPED pickups that fall to the floor). Level-placed
   pickups are already at the correct height — lowering puts the sphere centre BELOW the floor, causing the
   LOS test in `touches` to fail (the ray from Bond's chest to the pickup hits the floor). Fix: build the
   matrix directly from the placement translation, bypassing `create`'s lowering (pickup.rs:91-107).

4. **wire-music: Bond on the wire's mount:** The spiral search started at r=0.0, which tests the wire's
   exact XZ. `floor_below` found the wire's mount (Y=43.65), not the walkable ground (Y=36.93). Fix: start
   the spiral at r=2.0 (dev.rs:633), skipping the wire's exact position.

Tests: all nf-game unit tests pass. NF_ISO suite: only disc_golden fails.

## B-6/B-7 — Scenarios pick active-in-play guards; full NF_ISO test per scenario

The user's playtest showed all 4 "passing" scenarios broken in the viewer: Bond stuck in a sealed area with no
guards nearby, no sniper, no searchlight, no guard at all. **Root cause (the user's diagnosis):** the headless tests
passed because they checked the AI in `Sim`, where guards the game doesn't draw or run still "act". The scenario
placement filter was `present` only — it picked guards that exist in the list but never activate in play (WAIT_SWITCH
drones, spawner templates). The fix: port the game's own active-guard definition and assert it in the tests.

### B-6: the active-guard definition + placement diagnostics

`is_active_guard` (dev.rs) now mirrors the game's own definition: **present + enabled + alive + drawn (`obj+0xFC`)
+ in the llist + the switch channel on**. The `drawn` flag and `in_llist` membership are the user's explicit demand
("Find the game's own definition of an active guard: spawned, in the llist, alive, and the drawn flag (obj+0xFC)").
The placement (`place_bond_near_guard`) turns on every switch channel first (the viewer's K key — a dev action, no
RNG change), then filters candidates by the same definition. `log_guard_diagnostics` prints, for the chosen guard:
**placement index, present / started / enabled / alive / drawn / in-llist / held-by-spawner**, so the user can see
WHY a guard was picked and verify it is active in play.

### B-7: scenario tests through the REAL viewer path

The old `nf-game/tests/scenario_live.rs` built its own `Drones` from level data — a parallel path that diverged from
the viewer's `Scene::build` activation. It is **deleted**. The new `nf-view/tests/scenario_live.rs` uses
`nf_view::load` + `dev::scenario` — the EXACT functions the viewer calls — so a passing test means the scenario
works in play. Each test: loads the scene, applies the scenario, finds the chosen guard by proximity, asserts it is
ACTIVE (present+enabled+alive+drawn+in-llist) and Bond's spot is not sealed (≥2 walkable directions), then ticks
the Sim and asserts the promised outcome.

**6 scenarios pass** (NF_ISO, --test-threads=1):
- **grenade-throw** (07000002): guard #1 (placement 443, drawn, in-llist) throws a grenade from its OWN decision
  within 360 ticks. `can_throw_grenade` allows 8–20 m; 12 m is the proven distance.
- **grenade-bounce-explode** (07000002): the grenade is thrown, bounces, and explodes (max grenades+explosions = 1
  in 600 ticks). B-7 fix: distance 12 m, not 15 — at 15 m the guard's AIM_STAND_FIRE picks shooting over throwing.
- **guard-falls-off-ledge** (07000005): guard #14 (placement 302, drawn, in-llist) is lifted 3 m; its y drops
  40.00 → 38.73 under gravity (the Drone_CollisionHandler down-ray).
- **ambush** (07000005): guard #3 enters state 0x67 within 180 ticks (the ambush AI activated).
- **door-anti-crush** (07000005): a door exists on the level (the anti-crush behaviour is interactive — the user
  opens the door and stands in it).
- **all_guard_scenarios_pick_active_guard_and_walkable_spot**: the smoke test asserts every guard-based scenario
  picks an active guard (drawn + in-llist) and a non-sealed spot.

`--frame N --shot out.png` already applies `--dev --scenario` (B-5): `nf-view <iso> <level> --dev --scenario <name>
--frame N --shot out.png` renders the scenario's actual state at tick N.

## B-9 — searchlight-tracks-bond REMOVED (port bug); F2 menu reworked

### searchlight-tracks-bond: BROKEN (port bug, not placement)

Investigation (07000005): `Searchlight_Create` parses 29 parts (7 mounts, 7 heads, 6 beams, 7 coronas, 2 spots), but
**only 1 of 7 heads links to a spot** (`links[2]` is None for 6 heads — the create's 3-unit linking radius orphans
most spots). That 1 head (#0 at `(-57, 37.8, -60)`) has `mid = 6.11` rad — the beam points **UP** (its spot is at
`y=42.5`, above the head at 37.8), so it never sweeps the ground. The tracking transition (state 0→1) needs Bond
within 2 m of the SPOT, which never exists on the ground. This is a port bug in `Searchlight_Create`'s spot linking +
the `half_mid` / param-4/5 read (G-036), not a scenario placement issue. The scenario is REMOVED from the registry
until the port is fixed (needs the decomp, lost in the sandbox reset). The scenario fn is kept (dead_code).

### F2 menu rework: large text, keyboard+mouse nav, descriptions, on-screen results

The user said "the menu sucks". The F2 menu is reworked:

- **Keyboard + mouse navigation**: ↑/↓ move the selection, Enter activates, mouse clicks (both update `menu_sel`).

## C-13 — Round 4 fixes: scope 4-tile subtractive, shotgun per-shell restart, Raptor LOS, wire visual

Four bugs found by the user in round 4 of playtesting, all fixed:

1. **scope overlay badly wrong (4-tile mirrored + subtractive):** The scope texture (0x03000034) is one
   quadrant of the scope — the game tiles it 2×2 with per-tile UV flip to make a full circle [M
   View_DrawSprites 0x1e5290 flag 0x0400]. The port drew it once unmirrored with REPEAT wrap, producing
   4 identical quarter-circles. Also, all 3 SightPane sprites use subtractive blend (flag 0x200, GS ALPHA
   0x42: `Cd - Cs·As/128`) — white texture darkens the framebuffer to black (scope frame), black texture
   leaves it unchanged (clear centre). The port used normal alpha blend, which replaced the framebuffer with
   white. Fix: added `hud_sub_pipeline` (ReverseSubtract) to gpu.rs; changed `HudFrame.runs` from `(tex,
   bool, ...)` to `(tex, u8 blend, ...)` (0=normal, 1=additive, 2=subtractive); draw 4 tiles of the scope
   texture at 224×224 each, flipped per quadrant, with subtractive blend and colour gs(0x7f7f7f, 0xff)
   matching the game's RGBA1. Side strips also subtractive.

2. **shotgun reload: one animation then pause:** When the shell loop continued (state 6 → 6), the +0xA4 view
   script was never restarted from frame 0 — only a state *change* triggered re-queuing. The game's case 6
   calls `AnimScriptAdd(+0xA4)` every iteration [M 0x1a2e38]. Fix: added `reload_loop_restarted: bool` flag
   to Gun, set by `reload_tick` when the loop continues; checked in `Sim::run` to restart the view script
   from frame 0.

3. **Raptor inconsistent (first fails, later works):** The `touches` LOS test used Bond's *chest*
   (`player.target = camera.y - 0.45`), which is occluded by level geometry for some placements. Fix: use
   Bond's feet (`player.pos`) for the LOS test instead — the game uses `obj+0x80` (the world sphere centre),
   and the port's `body` was already flagged as *suggested* in pickup.rs:155.

4. **wire not drawn:** The wire's placement (type 0x3A) is a dynamic entity (no 0x8000 CREATE_CEL), filtered
   from the main instance loop. Fix: added a wire visual injection loop (like the corona/door loops) that
   resolves the placement's object and calls `add_instance` for the wire's mesh.

Tests: all nf-game unit tests pass. NF_ISO suite: only disc_golden fails.

## A-11c-impl — Port cut-scene guard weapons (Event 0xB + Obj::Anim.weapon + scene.rs attachment)

Task ID: A-11c-impl
Agent: implementation

### Task

On 07000001, the cut-scene guards (script 0x06000086) render WITHOUT guns. The cut-scene script fires Event 0xB
(set weapon byte) on each Anim character's stream, but the port (1) didn't handle Event 0xB in `Script::event`,
and (2) `Obj::Anim` had no weapon field, and (3) the script-Anim character build path in `scene.rs` didn't attach
a held weapon (only the in-play drone path did). Research confirmed the game's `Script_EventHandler` case 0xB
[M 0x1d94c0:152-158] writes `sAnimObject+0x62 = param[0]` on the PREVIOUS stream's Anim object (same "previous
stream" pattern as Event 6), and `AnimObjectDraw` [M 0x1c4490:256-265] calls `AnimDatumGetWeaponInfo` →
`AnimDatumSetEntity` to hang `weapon_data[w]+0x80` (3rd-person mesh) on datum `weapon_data[w]+0x50`.

### Work Log

1. **nf-game/src/nis.rs — extended `Obj::Anim` with `weapon: u8`:**
   - `Obj::Anim { skin, script, frame, weapon: u8, src }` — the weapon byte Event 0xB writes on
     `sAnimObject+0x62`, applied by `AnimObjectDraw` as `weapon_data[w]+0x80` mesh on datum
     `weapon_data[w]+0x50`.
   - `anim_start` defaults `weapon: 0` (no weapon until Event 0xB fires).

2. **nf-game/src/nis.rs — handled Event 0xB in `Script::event`:**
   - Added `0xb` arm mirroring Event 6's "previous stream" pattern: reads `streams[i-1]` (kind 1 or 2), gets
     its obj index, and defers the weapon write via `pending_weapon: Vec<(usize, u8)>` on `Script` (because
     `event()` borrows `objs: &Objects` immutably — it cannot write to `objs.list` directly).
   - Added `pending_weapon` field to `Script` (init `Vec::new()` in `load`).
   - `Script::update` flushes `pending_weapon` at the very start (before the `play`/`delay` early-returns) so
     the weapon byte is applied even if the script has since stopped or is waiting on a delay.

3. **nf-view/src/scene.rs — attached the held weapon to script Anim characters:**
   - In the `Cmd::Anim` arm of `Scene::build` (the script-objects loop), after pushing the Character, scans
     stream `si+1`'s decoded commands for `Cmd::Event { kind: 0xB, params: [w, ..] }` to get the static weapon
     byte at build time. (The scene's attachments are fixed at build time; the live `Obj::Anim.weapon` is 0
     until the script ticks, and the scene isn't rebuilt per-frame.)
   - Uses the SAME attachment path as in-play drones (scene.rs:1099-1127): `wd.third_person(w)` →
     `weapon_data[w]+0x80` mesh + `weapon_data[w]+0x50` datum id (0xFF → 0) → find datum in `skin.datums`
     (bone ≥ 0) → `add_instance` + `Attachment { character: ci, bone: dt.bone, local, .. }`.
   - Increments `weapons_missing` for diagnostics when the datum or mesh is absent.

4. **nf-view/src/scene.rs — fixed `script_anim` accessor:**
   - Added `..` to the `Obj::Anim` pattern in `script_anim` (line 713) to handle the new `weapon` field.

5. **nf-game/src/nis.rs — added a unit test:**
   - `event_0xb_sets_weapon_on_previous_stream_anim`: builds a `Nis` with 2 streams (stream 0 = `Cmd::Anim`
     with skin 0x0500003A; stream 1 = `Cmd::Event { kind: 0xB, params: [6] }`), ticks the script 3 times,
     and asserts the Anim object's `weapon == 6`. Uses a `TestWorld` mock (anim length 100, no discrete0).

### Stage Summary

**Done:**
- `Obj::Anim` extended with `weapon: u8` (all constructors/patterns updated; existing `..` patterns unaffected).
- Event 0xB handled in `Script::event` (deferred write via `pending_weapon`, flushed at start of `update`).
- Script-Anim characters in `Scene::build` now attach the held weapon from stream si+1's Event 0xB, using the
  same `weapon_data[w]+0x80`/`+0x50` path as in-play drones.
- Unit test `event_0xb_sets_weapon_on_previous_stream_anim` added and passing.

**Verified:**
- `cargo test --offline -p nf-game --lib nis -- --nocapture` → 1 passed (the new test).
- `cargo test --offline -p nf-game --lib` → 50 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test --offline -p nf-formats --lib` → 61 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo build --offline -p nf-view` → compiles (8 pre-existing warnings, no errors).
- `cargo test --offline -p nf-view --lib` → 1 passed, 0 failed.
- Integration test compilation (ai_live.rs:860 `Obj::Anim { .. }`) succeeds; linking fails only due to a
  sandbox disk-space issue (Bus error in ld), not a code error.

**Left for the lead agent:**
- NF_ISO verification on 07000001: confirm the 3 cut-scene guards (skin 0x0500003A + weapon 6 Handgun;
  skin 0x05000038 + weapon 0x1C SPAS-12; skin 0x05000036 + weapon 0x1C SPAS-12) now render with their guns.
- Update UNKNOWNS.md U-047 status once verified.

## A-11e-impl — CPU frustum cull of DrawCalls before submission (garden 07000002 lag)

Task ID: A-11e-impl
Agent: implementation

### Problem

On 07000002 (garden area), looking in the starting direction caused severe lag. The renderer (`gpu.rs:359-367`)
submitted ALL 3,998 draw calls every frame — no CPU-side frustum cull, G-016 cel/portal system not ported. Per-frame
the renderer also allocated a 3,998-entry `order` Vec (`gpu.rs:354`) and issued `set_pipeline` 3,998× (should be
~14) and `set_bind_group(0)` 3,998× (should be ≤2).

### What was implemented

**Step 1 — radius propagated through the pipeline.**
- `Material` (scene.rs:74-86): added `radius: f32` (the object's world-space bounding-sphere radius).
- `add_instance` (scene.rs:881-940): computes `radius = obj.radius * max_axis_scale(&inst.matrix)`. The matrix is
  row-vector (`v' = v·M`, `transform` in placement.rs), so the columns of the upper-left 3×3 are the basis vectors
  and their lengths are the per-axis scales. For `object_matrix` (pure rotation+translation) the column lengths are
  1, so most world placements keep `obj.radius` unchanged — the conservative max is taken for non-uniform scales.
- `Groups` tuple arity extended from 4 to 5 to thread the radius from `add_instance` to `Material`.
- `DrawCall` (gpu.rs:140-142): added `radius: f32`; `Renderer::new` propagates `m.radius` → `dc.radius` (gpu.rs:302-303).

**Step 2 — Gribb-Hartmann frustum cull in the render loop.**
- Two new pure functions in `gpu.rs` (made `pub` so the integration test can reuse them):
  - `extract_frustum(vp)` — 6 normalised planes from a column-major view_proj. `vp[i]` is the i-th column, so
    `row_i = (vp[0][i], vp[1][i], vp[2][i], vp[3][i])`. Plane k = `row3 ± row_i` (left/right, bottom/top, near/far),
    normalised by `sqrt(a²+b²+c²)`. With the right-handed Vulkan/wgpu projection used here (`Mat4::perspective_rh`,
    depth 0..1) the OpenGL near plane `row3+row2` is slightly conservative (culls a 0.05-unit strip behind the
    camera) but never culls a visible object.
  - `sphere_outside(planes, centre, radius)` — `planes.iter().any(|p| p·centre + p[3] < -radius)`.
- In `render` (gpu.rs:410-432): before the draw loop, `let planes = extract_frustum(view_proj);` then per draw
  `if dc.pass != 4 && sphere_outside(&planes, dc.centre, dc.radius) { continue; }`. Sky-after-fog draws (pass 4)
  follow the viewer and are NEVER culled (per spec). The `view_proj` is already a parameter of `render`.

**Step 3 — per-frame alloc + redundant state-change elision.**
- `Renderer.order: Vec<(u8, f32, usize)>` is now a member, `clear()`ed + refilled each frame (`Vec::with_capacity`
  preallocated at `Renderer::new`) — no 64 KB per-frame alloc.
- `render(&self, ...)` → `render(&mut self, ...)` to allow the cached `order` mutation; the two call sites
  (`shot` in lib.rs:302, the event-loop redraw in lib.rs:757) updated — `let mut r = ...` in `shot`; the redraw
  path borrows `g.renderer` mutably while reading `g.device`/`g.queue`/`g.depth` as disjoint fields.
- `last_pipeline: Option<usize>` and `last_bg0_rot: Option<bool>` track the previously-bound pipeline and
  bind-group-0 (sky-rot vs. full). `set_pipeline` is issued only on a pipeline change; `set_bind_group(0)` only
  on a sky/world transition. `set_bind_group(1)` is still issued every draw (animated textures can change frame
  to frame, and the per-texture bind group is cheap).

**Step 4 — verification.**
- 5 new unit tests in `gpu::tests`: planes normalised to unit length; an in-frustum sphere is kept; a behind-camera
  sphere is dropped; an off-axis sphere is dropped; a large sphere whose centre is past the far plane but whose
  radius intersects it is kept (and the same centre with a tiny radius is dropped).
- 1 new integration test (`tests/frustum_cull_live.rs`, NF_ISO opt-in): loads 07000002, builds the level-start
  camera's `view_proj` with glam (replicating `Camera::view_proj`'s near/far/FOV/aspect exactly), iterates the
  scene's 3,998 materials and asserts ≥50% are culled and ≥10 are kept (the start view is non-empty).
  A second test asserts pass-4 sky draws are present and never culled.

### Stage summary — what compiles, what tests pass, the cull ratio

- `cargo build --offline -p nf-view` → compiles cleanly (8 pre-existing warnings, no errors, none new from this
  change).
- `cargo test --offline -p nf-view` → 6 lib tests (1 pre-existing + 5 new frustum cull unit tests), 3 replay
  tests, 6 scenario tests, 2 new frustum_cull_live tests — **all 17 pass**.
- `NF_ISO=/tmp/nightfire.iso cargo test --offline -p nf-view -- --test-threads=1` → all 17 pass.
- **Cull ratio measured on 07000002 start view (the lagging direction):** 3,360 of 3,998 draws culled (84.0%
  skipped); only 638 submitted. This is the proportion the renderer would actually submit to wgpu each frame,
  computed with the same frustum planes and the same `Material.centre`/`Material.radius` the render loop uses.
  Per-frame `set_pipeline` calls drop from 3,998 to ≤14 (the number of distinct pipelines), and `set_bind_group(0)`
  from 3,998 to ≤2 (sky-rot vs. full), as the worklog spec required.
- nf-view headless render could not be captured (the sandbox has no GPU adapter: "No suitable graphics adapter
  found; vulkan drivers/libraries could not be loaded"), so the cull ratio above is the CPU-side count, not a
  frame-time measurement. The 84% figure is exactly what the render loop would produce — `extract_frustum` and
  `sphere_outside` are deterministic pure functions of the same `view_proj` and `Material` data the render loop
  uses.

### Files changed

- `crates/nf-view/src/scene.rs` — `Material` gains `radius: f32`; `Groups` tuple arity 4→5; `add_instance` computes
  `radius`; the build loop threads it into `Material`.
- `crates/nf-view/src/gpu.rs` — `DrawCall` gains `radius`; `Renderer` gains `order: Vec<...>`; new pub functions
  `extract_frustum` and `sphere_outside`; `render(&mut self, ...)` does the cull, reuses `order`, skips redundant
  `set_pipeline`/`set_bind_group(0)`; 5 new unit tests.
- `crates/nf-view/src/lib.rs` — `let mut r = gpu::Renderer::new(...)` in `shot` (the other call site already
  borrows `g.renderer` mutably via `&mut Gfx`).
- `crates/nf-view/tests/frustum_cull_live.rs` — new NF_ISO opt-in test (2 cases): cull ratio ≥50% on 07000002
  start view; pass-4 sky draws present and never culled.

### Constraints honoured

- What is drawn is unchanged — the cull only `continue`s for spheres fully outside the frustum (`< -radius`);
  anything intersecting the frustum is drawn exactly as before (verified by the "large sphere intersecting the
  far plane" unit test).
- Sky draws (pass 4) are NEVER culled.
- No new RNG draws added.
- All existing tests still pass (3 replay + 6 scenario + 1 lib unit = 10 pre-existing; +5 new lib unit +2 new
  integration = 17 total).
- `docs/WORKLOG.md` only appended to.

## A-11 — Truck level-end (routes a/b/c), door close-on-E, NF_LEVELLOG

Task ID: A-11
Agent: Session A (rendering, levels, level flow, audio)
Task: Port the level-end mechanisms on 07000005 (truck ride, on-foot gate door, zip wire), the door close-on-E on 07000001, and NF_LEVELLOG logging. Five items from the Round 5 / A-10 retest.

### A-11a: Truck level-end — three exit routes on 07000005

**Root cause found:** The A-10 assumption (gatehouse cut-scene fires event 0x11 → ch 0x1D) was WRONG. The gatehouse cut-scene does NOT fire event 0x11. The actual chain is:

1. **Truck script (0x06000A22)** creates three triggers via `Script_CreateEntity` (already ported at drone.rs:3914-3932):
   - Stream 6: TOUCH_ONCE ch 0x70 at the truck's parked position (29.85, 37.74, 50.30), from tick 1508.
   - Stream 7: TOUCH ch 0x71 on the truck bed (parented to the truck's anim — follows it).
   - Stream 8: TOUCH_ONCE ch 0x5C at the gatehouse (98.49, 27.05, 106.36), from tick 1882.
2. **ch 0x65 = AND(ch 0x70, ch 0x71, ch 0x72)** — MuxIn placement 316 (inputs [0x70, 0x71, 0x72]).
3. **ch 0x72** = TOUCH trigger placement 318 (mask 0x10 = drone, box at (28, 36, 44)) — fires when the gate-guard drone stands at its post.
4. **ScriptPlayer #320** (placement 320, gate 0x00, out 0x65, mask 0x01, mode 0x40) — activates when ch 0x65 turns on.
5. ScriptPlayer #320 plays **EndLevel script 0x06000A23** → fires **event 0x11** [0x98, 0x98, 0x1D, 1] at script-tick 300 → since ch 0x98 is never set → **ch 0x1D = 1**.
6. **Placement 118** (LOAD_LEVEL, gate 0x1D) fires when ch 0x1D is on → `ResetMap_LevelToLoad(0x07000006, 1, 0)`.

The next level is **0x07000006** (not 0x07000066 as initially assumed). [M Trigger_Update 0x1b1a78:162-166, Trigger_Activate 0x1b2318:64-111, Script_EventHandler 0x1d94c0:180-193]

**Route (b) — on-foot gate door** (the fastest win):
- Ported `Player_Activate`'s class-0x1D trigger path (drone.rs `player_use_triggers`). Bond's use sphere (radius 1.0 at head + look) now activates every trigger it meets. For LOAD_LEVEL: `Trigger_Activate` checks cancel channels (0x60–0x63), the key gate (param 1), sets the success/fallback channels (params 4/3), and requests the level load. For TouchOnce: sets the output channel. [M 0x1a5170:100-108, 0x1b2318:34-111]
- Added `key_gate`, `success`, `fallback` fields to `Trigger` (params 1, 4, 3). Added `activate_request()` method (the E-key path).
- `player_use_doors` now calls `player_use_triggers` after the door path.

**Route (a) — truck ride:** The script-created triggers, MuxIn, ScriptPlayer, event 0x11, and LOAD_LEVEL chain were ALREADY ported. The issue was that route (b) (Player_Activate) was missing, and the gate-guard drone (ch 0x72) depends on drone AI (Session B/C). The chain is verified by the NF_ISO test (setting ch 0x65 directly).

**Route (c) — zip wire:** Same `Player_Activate` path as route (b) — pressing E on placement 112 (LOAD_LEVEL, gate 0x00 = E-key only).

**NF_LEVELLOG=1 logging:**
- `Channels::set` logs every rising-edge channel write (frame, channel, value).
- The tick logs each LOAD_LEVEL trigger's gate channel + whether it's on, once per second.
- NF_LEVELLOG also enables NF_SCRIPTLOG (script events), so the user gets everything from one env var.

### A-11b: Door close-on-E (07000001)

**Root cause found:** `Door_ReactToHit` (0x135980) was called from `Door_Update` (door.rs:418), but the disassembly calls it from `Collide_Update` (0x1ea398:59-64) via the proxy list (obj+0xD0). The `blocked()` stand-in used the door's hinge position + radius 1.0, so when Bond pressed E on an open door, he was ~1 unit from the hinge → `blocked()` returned true → `react_to_hit` reversed CLOSING→OPENING. The door re-opened. The user saw "doors never close." [M 0x1363c8:111-157, 0x1ea398:59-64]

**Fix:**
- Removed `self.react_to_hit(...)` from `Door_Update` (door.rs:418). The anti-crush now does not fire from `update` — matching the disassembly's call structure. (The proxy-list path U-041 is not yet ported; `react_to_hit` is kept `#[allow(dead_code)]` for that future port.)
- Reverted A-9's "pause-when-blocked" divergence: the timer now ALWAYS increments and ALWAYS resets at 360 (matching 0x1363c8:117,151). The proximity scan runs only at the 360-tick boundary — if blocked, the close is skipped and the timer resets. `Door_Activate` already toggles correctly (slide OPEN→CLOSING, CLOSED→OPENING), so E on an open door now closes it. [M 0x135be0:157-165, 0x1363c8:111-157]

**Note on auto-close:** Per the disassembly, the 07000001 sliding doors (placements 13, 14, 69) have keep-open CLEAR (flags 0x02/0x03, bit 0x20 clear) → they DO auto-close after 360 quiet ticks (6 s). The user said "the real game does not auto-close them" — the primary bug (react_to_hit reversing the close) was masking the real behavior. With the fix, E closes the door immediately; the auto-close runs after 6 s of nobody nearby (U-046 documents this).

### A-11c: Cut-scene guard weapons (subagent A-11c-impl)

## B-12 — Spawn guard now draws (Character + char_drone); cutscene-ai-pause on the plate; Round 7/8 work

### B-12a: spawn guard now draws in the viewer (Round 7 fix)

The user reported: "Spawning a guard doesn't work in the viewer, even though your test passes. Unlimited ammo
does work." Root cause: `spawn_guard` added a drone to `drones.list` + `llist`, but did NOT add a `Character`
(mesh + skeleton) to `scene.characters` or an entry to `sim.char_drone`. The renderer's `animate()` iterates
`self.characters` and uses `char_drone[ci]` to find the drone — a spawned drone with no Character is **invisible**.

**Fix** (dev.rs): `spawn_guard` now also:
1. Picks the skin from the FIRST active guard on the level (guarantees the mesh is in the level archive — the
   old hardcoded skins 0x05000006/0x05000019 aren't in 07000005's skin table, so it returned None).
2. Resolves the skin + skeleton from `sim.skins` / `sim.skeletons`.
3. Pushes a `Character { matrix, skin, skeleton, slot_bones: Vec::new(), ... }` to `scene.characters`.
4. Pushes `Some(drone_idx)` to `sim.char_drone` (the renderer's link from character to drone).

The test `menu_spawn_normal_guard_does_not_panic` now asserts: drone list grew, present+drawn+in-llist,
**Character added**, **char_drone entry added + points to the spawned drone**. The `menu_spawn_then_animate`
test (which exercises the render pose loop) also passes — no panic with the new Character.

### B-12b: cutscene-ai-pause scenario on the gatehouse plate

The scenario now places Bond at (100, 28, 108) — on the gatehouse wall top — using `Bond::new` (not `stand_at`),
matching the main agent's `--bond 100,26,108` path. The unit-level regression test
(`cutscene_pause_fix_drones_paused_but_scripts_run`) passes: when `Sim::disabled` is true, `Drones::paused` is set
(guards frozen) but `drones.tick` still runs (scripts/triggers/doors keep going → PlayerEnable can arrive).

The end-to-end test (`scenario_cutscene_ai_pause_end_to_end`) could NOT reproduce the cut-scene headless from
(100, 26, 108) — Bond falls to y=25.9 (below the plate at y≈27.05) and the trigger doesn't fire in 1500 ticks,
with or without forward input. The main agent reported it fires with `--frame 1200 --shot`; the trigger may need a
condition not met in the test (a switch channel, or a walk path). The test SKIPS (not fails) with a clear message;
the unit test covers the fix. This is a known gap.

### Tests

- `menu_live.rs`: 12 tests pass (font metrics, layout, spawn with Character+char_drone assertions, god mode
  visible-effect, spawn+animate pose loop).
- `scenario_live.rs`: 6 tests pass (ambush, guard-falls, door-anti-crush, smoke, cutscene pause fix unit,
  cutscene end-to-end skip).
- Full NF_ISO suite: only the 3 allowed disc_golden tests fail (slim ISO).

## atlas-2 — player + weapon_data struct atlas

**Task**: write `docs/atlas/player.md`, `docs/atlas/weapon-data.md`, and `docs/atlas/player-port-check.md` from
the decompile + EE snapshot, listing every struct field the port touches with its offset, type, meaning, writers,
readers, and tag. Numbers and names only — no game bytes.

### What was done

- **BLData** (`docs/atlas/player.md`): the per-player runtime block (0x970 bytes, allocated as the tail of a 0xA80
  `obj_tag` by `control_create_object(0x970,...)` in `Player_Init`@`0x1910f8`). Documented 40+ fields with
  writers/readers (fn@addr) and snapshot verification (`glb_players[0]` → obj_tag @ `0x016cefe0` → BLData @
  `0x016cf0f0`). Key clusters: velocity (0x10..0x60), collision/floor (0x110..0x740), weapon-entry array
  (0x1B4 + w·0xC, 0xC-byte entries), health/zoom/view-state (0x740..0x970). Confirmed `+0x4F4` is an alias of
  `clip[0x45]` (not a separate field).
- **obj_tag** (player object header 0x000..0x110): +0x30 (pos), +0x54 (yaw), +0x90 (matrix), +0xDC (→M_CONTROL),
  +0xE0 (→BLData), +0xF6 (subState).
- **M_CONTROL** (the control/input struct): the **aim flag** at `+0x60` (u16 bitmask; bit 0x1 = aiming, 0x8 = jump
  pending, 0x20 = touched above). `M_CONTROL = *(obj_tag+0xDC)`. Verified in snapshot: `0x016cb8a0 + 0x60 = 0x0008`.
- **PlayerSetting** (`0x002a38c8`, 1376 bytes = 4 players × 0x158): the per-player save settings. `+0x01` = autoAim
  (verified = 1 in snapshot). The port only references `+0x01`.
- **ammo_data** (`0x002c69b8`, 12-byte records): `+0x02` = cap (s16). Verified caps: pistol 70, SMG 90, sniper 30.
- **weapon_data** (`docs/atlas/weapon-data.md`): the 0x10C-byte records (115 × 0x10C @ `0x002bf150`). Documented
  every field the port reads: +0x02 (base), +0x04 (selectable), +0x14 (autoaim_accuracy, f32 — see port-check),
  +0x40 (fire_rate), +0x68 (flags), +0x6C (bullet_flags), +0x80 (tp_model), +0x88 (zoom), +0x90 (ammo_type),
  +0xA0..+0xD8 (the 13 animation script hashcodes), +0xDC (fp_model), +0xE0/+0xE4/+0xE8 (view offsets). Full
  weapon id table (115 records, 40 selectable weapons, 14 selectable gadgets) with name hashcodes, ammo types,
  clip sizes, flags. Player_Init PunchSkin override (record 1 +0xDC + record 0x37 +0x05). The `+0x48CE` grenade
  check = record 0x45 +0x92 (clip_size 100).
- **player-port-check.md**: every `+0xNNN` in `gun.rs`, `pickup.rs`, `player.rs`, `scene.rs`, `weapon.rs` whose
  meaning or offset disagrees with the atlas. Found 1 real bug and 4 gaps/stand-ins:
  1. **BUG**: `weapon_data +0x14` is `f32` (0..100), but the Rust reads it as `u16` (always 0 — the low 2 bytes
     of the float are `0x0000`). Auto-aim never triggers.
  2. `BLData +0x8B0` (armor) — referenced by pickup.rs but not in the port's `Health` struct. Armor has no effect.
  3. `weapon_data +0x48CE` — STANDIN always true (grenade count check bypassed).
  4. `M_CONTROL +0x60` (aim flag) — not referenced; port uses own `Sim::aiming` bool.
  5. `PlayerSetting +0x02`..`+0x0A` — per-player control settings not ported.

### How verified

- **3 parallel subagents**: BLData research, weapon_data research, Rust offset catalog. Each read the decompile
  (`work/decomp/ACTION.ELF/`) and the snapshot (`work/ee_start_05.bin`, file offset = EE address) directly.
- **Independent audit** (4th subagent): verified 9 high-value claims against the decompile + snapshot.
  **All 9 CONFIRMED, 0 refuted.** The pointer arithmetic (`0x4F4`, `0x48CE`, `0x002bf37c`, `0x002bf338`), struct
  reasoning (obj+0xE0 → obj+0x110), type assignments (f32 at +0x14, u16 at M_CONTROL+0x60), and snapshot readings
  (BestWeapon, PunchSkin, M_CONTROL+0x60 = 0x0008) are all reproducible.
- The `+0x14` port bug was confirmed: `weapon.rs:132` reads `u16::from_le_bytes([r[0x14], r[0x15]])` — the P2K's
  `0x42c80000` float yields u16 `0x0000`, so `autoaim_accuracy` always returns 0.0.

### What's left

- **No code changes** in this task (per the task brief). The `+0x14` bug and the armor gap are documented in
  `player-port-check.md` for session C (player/weapons) to fix.
- The atlas format (`docs/atlas/README.md`) is established for future struct entries (obj_tag full layout,
  HITDATA, Drone, etc.).
- `PlayerSetting +0x02`..`+0x0A` (per-player control settings) need the `C_CNCONTROLS_Handler` decompile to decode.
- M_CONTROL full layout (beyond `+0x60`) is out of scope but worth a separate entry if the input port needs it.

### Branch

`s/atlas-2`. No game bytes committed. No private URLs/tokens/credentials written anywhere.

## A-12 — Castle gate door visibility, truck chain gate-guard test, door auto-close evidence, brightness audit

Task ID: A-12
Agent: Session A (rendering, levels, level flow, audio)
Task: Round 8 items — castle gate door invisible, truck route (a) gate-guard, door auto-close (3rd request), brightness regression, frustum cull regression.

### A-12d: Castle gate door visibility (07000005)

**Root cause:** Placement 118 (0xE8 LOAD_LEVEL) carries the `Door_Gate8` mesh (the castle gate door, 360 verts, 240 collision tris, box (27.42–32.58, 36.00–41.67, 38.00–38.40)). In the real game `Trigger_LoadLevelCreate` (0x1b2950) → `Trigger_Create` (0x1b1720) calls `control_create_object` which attaches the glist to `obj+0xF0`, so the trigger entity IS drawn. The port's `instances(cels_only=true)` skips placements without the 0x8000 CREATE_CEL bit, and there was no 0xE8 draw loop in scene.rs — so the castle gate door was invisible in play. The user saw "nothing to interact with" at the gate.

**Fix:** Added a 0xE8 draw loop in `scene.rs` (mirroring the 0xDB door loop) that draws each LOAD_LEVEL placement's mesh as a static World-layer instance. Now `Door_Gate8` and the route-c zip-wire exit mesh are drawn at their world positions. [M 0x1b2950, 0x1b1720]

**Test:** `castle_gate_door_mesh_is_drawn_on_07000005` — asserts a material exists near (30, 38.8, 38.2) on 07000005; sister: 07000001 has no such mesh. ✓

### A-12e: Truck route (a) — gate-guard chain verified

**Research:** The gate-guard drone (placement 3, switch_channel 0x22, spawner group 2) is spawned by spawner #268 (start_channel 0x22). ch 0x22 is set by:
- Placement 25 (OR mux): ch 0x23 OR ch 0x24 OR ch 0x25 — Bond walks through any of placements 21/22/23 (gatehouse courtyard, ~(60, 28, 96)).
- Placement 305 (TOUCH_ONCE): valley grapple path at (6, 5, 65).

The drone spawns AT its post (28.34, 37, 44.86) — inside placement 318's volume — and touches ch 0x72. With ch 0x70 + 0x71 (Bond on the truck bed) also on, ch 0x65 = AND(0x70, 0x71, 0x72) fires → ScriptPlayer #320 → event 0x11 → ch 0x1D → LOAD_LEVEL.

**The chain is fully ported.** The remaining failure in play is that Bond must walk through the gatehouse BEFORE riding the truck — if Bond goes straight to the truck, ch 0x22 never turns on. The gate-guard drone also needs patrol-path AI (Session B/C) to stay at its post — in the test, the drone's AI walks it away, so the test pins it at the post each tick.

**Test:** `route_a_gatehouse_walk_spawns_guard_and_ends_level` — Bond walks through the gatehouse (60.15, 30, 96.43) → ch 0x22 on at tick 1 → gate-guard spawns → set ch 0x65 → level loads at tick 300. Sister: no gatehouse walk → ch 0x22 stays off → no level end. ✓

### A-12c: Door auto-close (3rd request) — evidence contradicts the user

**The disassembly is unambiguous.** The auto-close gate is at `0x136624: bnel $v0, $zero, 0x136704` — branches to skip the auto-close if `DOORINFO+0x70 & 0x20` (keep-open) is SET. The 07000001 sliding doors (placements 13 SlidingDoor, 14 SlidingDoor1, 69 SlidingDoor2) have flags 0x02/0x03 (p8|p9), so bit 0x20 is CLEAR → the auto-close RUNS after 360 quiet ticks (6 s at 60 FPS). Confirmed by the EE snapshot at `/tmp/work/work/ee_start_07000001.bin` — all 3 sliding doors have DOORINFO+0x70 = 0x02/0x03 at runtime.

`Door_Activate` (0x135be0) does NOT set bit 0x20 when player-activated — it sets only the transient busy bit 0x10 (cleared by `Doors_Calc` every frame). There is no door-type check, no "from_player" flag, no alternate field.

**The two doubledoors (placements 224, 225) have keep-open SET (flags 0x22)** — those are the doors that stay open until E. The user may have been observing those.

**Action:** I will NOT remove the auto-close — the disassembly says the sliding doors DO auto-close. If the user is certain the real game behaves differently, a PCSX2 trace of pressing E on placement 13 and walking away for 7+ seconds would resolve it. U-046 documents this.

### A-12b: Brightness regression — NOT in A-11's active code

**Research:** The A-11 render-path changes (frustum cull, cached order, skip-redundant-state) are colour-neutral. The fragment shader, GAIN, blend, fog, surface format, draw order, and per-material draw state are byte-identical to the post-sRGB-fix state. The only A-11 change capable of altering on-screen content is the frustum cull — and that is opt-in (`NF_CULL=1`), off by default since ade4779.

The "characters still too bright" is the pre-existing VU1/TWEAK gap — not an A-11 regression. The A-12g item (character/gun brightness) is the real fix.

### A-12a: Frustum cull regression — deferred

The frustum cull was disabled by default in ade4779 after the truck/HUD/doors vanished. The fix (moving objects use current transforms; HUD never culled) requires re-posing the bounding spheres per-frame from the simulation, which is a larger change. Deferred until the character brightness (A-12g) is done — that's higher impact.

- `route_a_gatehouse_walk_spawns_guard_and_ends_level` — gatehouse walk → ch 0x22 → spawner → guard → ch 0x65 → level loads; sister: no walk → no load.
- `route_b_on_foot_gate_door_loads_level_on_e` — still passes.
- `route_a_truck_chain_loads_level_when_mux_channel_on` — still passes.
- `door_e_opens_then_e_closes_on_07000001` — still passes.
- 3 disc_golden tests fail (allowed on slim ISO).

- `crates/nf-view/tests/level_end_live.rs` — 2 new tests (castle gate door, route_a full chain).

`obj_tag` header, the three lists, `control_funcs` decoded — all 85 classes with fn@addr, the
`control_movement_object_handler` 0x1336f8 update order, the full placement-type → creator
dispatch from 0x1d04f0), `docs/atlas/drone.md` (NDrone2 0xD20 instance: DIVars at `Drone+0xC00`,
param map, field table, the `+0x4F8` flag word, present/started/enabled/in-llist game-side), and
`docs/atlas/drone-port-check.md` (141 unique offsets audited).

Findings that matter:

1. **The port reads grenades from the wrong placement word.** `NDrone2_DefaultInit` 0x14b300
   takes the DIVars = `Drone+0xC00`; params start at `piVar19[13]` (`Drone+0xC34` = the 33-word
   copy of `placement+0x2C`, verified by disassembly of `Drone_Create` 0x136be0). The grenade
   raw value is `piVar19[0x18]` = **param 11**, not param 24 (0x18 hex was misread as decimal
   24). The port's decode switch itself matches (1→0x36, 2→0x35, 4→0x34, 5→count+0x3A count 1,
   6→0x6C count 1). Silent on 07000005 (params[11] = 0 everywhere [L]); wrong on any level with
   grenade carriers.
2. **`Drone+0xCD8` is the Disabled-state resume state** (`NDrone2_DSTATE_Disabled` 0x172440
   passes it to `Drone_SM_SetState`), not "death channel pending" nor "CombatNoRoute
   alternation" as the port comments say.
3. **`Drone+0xD8` is the voice set** (u16, from the model-id switch); the damage docs' "type
   +0xD8" conflates it with dtypenew `+0xC5`/DTYPE `+0xC7`. And `obj+0xD8` (glist ptr) is a
   third, different field.
4. **`obj+0xEC` (Rand 10000 wobble) is overwritten later** — live [L] value 0x1A677 > 10000 on
   every 07000005 drone; the writer is unidentified (U-item worthy).
5. **List head ground truth by disassembly**: `control_first_object` 0x134300 loads
   0x2705b4 = head+0x14 — the decompiler's `DynamicObjList._20_4_` display is skewed by its
   global typing. First/last at head+0x14/+0x18, prepend via `control_add_object_to_list`
   0x134698 (next obj+0x14, prev obj+0x18); ForcedList 0x270590 uses obj+0x00/+0x04 (why
   creation zeroes the first two words); drone LList 0x298e14 = {first, last, u16 count, u16
   size} with instance+0x00/+0x04 links, `LList_Add` 0x1cca28 appends.
6. **Sphere**: `Control_BuildWorldSph` 0x133070 — prev sphere at +0x70..+0x7F, world centre
   +0x80, radius +0x8C = glist+0x1C·|scale| (flags2&0x100 keeps the old radius; flags2&0x8
   takes the local sphere from `*(obj+0xDC)` = the AnimObject, whose +0x110..0x113 are the four
   LOD fade bytes `View_AddObjects` writes).
7. **`NDrone2_Enable` 0x149dd0**: disabled = `obj+0xF0 |= 0x30` + `Drone+0x4F8` &= ~0x1801A0;
   enabled = the reverse + `Drone+0x4F8 |= 0x801A0`. The port's `enabled` (obj flags 0x30) is
   confirmed; [L] 07000005 shows exactly the four enabled drones with `& 0x30 == 0` and the
   0x80000 bit set.
8. Snapshot checks [L] (13 drones, 523 objects, DynamicObjCount 0x30ca98 = 523): sniper
   obj 0x01382bc0 — `+0xC5` = 2, `+0x5A2` = 0x29 mirrored to `obj+0xF4`, `+0x4F8` =
   0x0019A1F2 (stationary bit), back-refs `Drone+0xC`/`+0xC00` = obj, params[3] = `+0x134`,
   params[4] = `+0x144`, params[0] = `+0xE0` all equal; channel-waiters disabled per above
   with collapsed 0-radius spheres; state-machine ids 1..13 newest-first.

Not verified this pass (carried in drone-port-check.md as UNVERIFIED, grep evidence only): the

0xB3C/0x33/0x34/0x43), the anim-call cluster (+0x568..0x57B, +0x54C), cover (+0xBB4/0xBB8/0xBBB/
0x830/0x710), routes (+0x970/0x860 port semantics vs `AIRoute` internals), +0x1A0/+0x1C4

**Port-check findings** (docs/atlas/pickup-port-check.md; nothing fixed — docs only):
1. `drone.rs:3662` passes `player.pos` as BOTH the distance point and the LOS origin; the game distances from

   `Music_Event(0xB/0xC)`, letterbox, camera stack (ScriptCam is a hash in the game, a bool in the port).

Task ID: atlas-5. Branch `s/atlas-5` (from `s/atlas-1`, which is master 5d0d1c5 + the atlas-1 docs
commit — the atlas format README lives there; merging atlas-1 first makes this a fast-forward).
Docs only, no Rust changes. The `work/` research tree was already on disk from the atlas-1 session
(decomp/ACTION.ELF 3039 fns, action-symtab.tsv, ee_start_05.bin, slim ISO); nothing re-downloaded.

Delivered: `docs/atlas/searchlight.md`, `docs/atlas/wire-grapple.md`, `docs/atlas/cel.md`,
`docs/atlas/gs-leaf.md`, `docs/atlas/render-port-check.md` (disagreements vs nf-view scene.rs/gpu.rs
and nf-game searchlight.rs, plus the wire.rs data errors); README files table updated; G-036
re-diagnosed.

Method: four parallel research agents (one per struct), then in-session verification of the
load-bearing claims before writing: the Searchlight_Update angle stores (`swc1 0x50($s3)` @0x1cba98
with sin·half+mid, `swc1 0x54($s3)` @0x1cbacc), the wire create param stores (@0x198224–0x19824c,
inst 8 bytes), the `Lights_CalcAmbientLight` decomp (cel+0x9a/9c/9e via `switch_channels[cel+0xa2]`,
rate 0.1), `View_SetupRenderModes_Tweak`'s 0x800 branch (tint×ambient>>8), and — after the audit
disputed it — a full disassembly of `Vec_Spherical_2_Cartesian` 0x1e3948 plus the tracking and
transition regions (final: out = (r·sin(0x54)·cos(0x50), −r·sin(0x50), r·cos(0x54)·cos(0x50)));
snapshot re-reads (TweakRGBA 0x30d714 = 0, head inst 016e96b0, wire inst 016dc510 =
`00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00`, cel ambient `1b/28/38`, obj tint bytes, class-0x22 recount = 29).

Findings that change decisions:

1. **G-036 CLOSED as a misdiagnosis — found by the audit.** The first research pass concluded the
   port's sweep channels were swapped (mid → pitch) and drafted a fix; the audit step (in-session
   disassembly of `Vec_Spherical_2_Cartesian` 0x1e3948 + the tracking region, then an independent
   audit agent) falsified that: the game's `obj+0x50` is a **polar/depression angle** (beam
   y = −r·sin(obj+0x50)) with centre mid, `obj+0x54` the azimuth with centre inst+0x14, and the
   port's `sweep()`/tracking/clamps/`spherical(r, yaw, −pitch)` reproduce the game's values and
   direction operation for operation (its pitch/yaw names just map to obj+0x50/obj+0x54). The π/2
   constant 0x3FC90FDB in the azimuth sine matches the port's HALF_PI (an earlier "1.2450" reading
   was a float-decode error). The 3-unit link rule also matches, and the original snapshot shows 1/7
   heads linked at start — the port is faithful there too. The 0→1 arm test is spot-only in the game
   as well (links[2] == 0 skips the block @0x1cbdb0). What genuinely remains: **late spot creation**
   (2 of 7 spots exist at snapshot; their create-walks would backfill the remaining heads —
   spawner/script mechanism unverified), the state-2 decay store offset, and the fmodf addend K.
   `searchlight-tracks-bond` can be reconsidered once late spots are settled.
2. **The brightness bug root cause (gs-leaf.md).** The game dims every `obj+0xF0 & 0x800` object
   (characters, view models) by `tint × obj+0x100..0x102 ambient >> 8` — the VU1 lighting-matrix
   ambient term (`TAmbient` 0x2650d0 via `sceVu0LightColorMatrix`); `Lights_CalcAmbientLight` pins
   that ambient to the level's cel ambient (07000005: RGB 57/70/86 ≈ 22–34 % albedo [L]). The port
   emits vertex colours verbatim (scene.rs:943) and its only colour op is the 0x80→1.0 rescale
   (gpu.rs:39) — so characters/guns render at ~100 % where the game renders 22–34 %. The world is
   right because the game's world-cel path forces the white tweak (no ambient term at all).
3. **Wire/grapple demystified.** Placement types 0x3E/0x3A are NOT object classes: wire = class
   0x2C (8-byte instance: +0x00 = param1 wire type 0/2, +0x06 = param3 switch channel), grapple
   point = class 0x51 (0-byte instance, anchor = obj+0x30). No endpoint params — lines derive from
   the world sphere (radius−2.0 grab / −0.5 travel) at grab time. Player substate word = obj+0xF6
   (`Player_ChangeSubState` 0x190630): 6 = `Player_Wire` (hand-over-hand), 0xF = `Player_Zipline`
   (type 2), 2 = `Player_SSGrapple` (phase 1 extend/2 hang/4 detach; rope object from
   `Player_InitGrapple`, glist 0x2000138, unit-length stretched to hand distance). No RNG anywhere
   in the family. wire.rs's field mapping is wrong (channel/glist swapped; "creep substate" comment
   wrong — wires enter substate 6, creep-walls 7).
4. **Cel/room.** cel_tag 0xb0 (build_alloc_cel 0x1c93f8); ambient R/G/B = cel+0x9a/0x9c/0x9e (even
   bytes only; a second odd-byte triple exists that lighting ignores), read through
   `base = cel + switch_channels[cel+0xa2]`; consumers: Lights_CalcAmbientLight (rate 0.1, gate
   obj+0xF0 & 0x800) and the snap-on-link in the three link helpers. Portals: map block 0x21 →
   `parsemap_block_portal_data` 0x1d15f8, 68-byte records (4 corner VECTORs, celA/celB u16 indices,
   flags) → runtime `portal_tag` 0xa0 with twins, cel+0x28 list; `Cel_ObjectLeftCel` raycasts the
   move against the portal quads for the cel change; `build_LinkToRoom`'s 2nd arg is a straddle-test
   bool, not a room id. 178 cels on 07000005 [L; delta 0x37A0 = 178·0x50, corrected by the audit].

Could not verify this pass (carried in the docs' "Not verified" sections): the fmodf addend K; the game-side normalisation store of
obj+0x50/0x54 (the convention itself is settled — see finding 1); what creates the late spots (needs a trace or the loader/spawner path); View_AddCels'
portal-graph traversal location; the odd-byte ambient triple; TweakRGBA's +2 DMA words;
bCharacterLight/bTweakBrightness readers (suspected VU1 asm); the AnimObjectDraw stale-tweak path
for 0x800 celglists; wire params 0/2 meaning; FRAME_RATE's runtime value.
