**The floor quads are identified.** The user's flat light-blue quads near stairs and railings (07000007+) are the
level's baked shadow-decal objects: `hall_shadows1/3/4`, `OBJECT_banistershadows1..4`, `hall_shadow_banister01/02`
[D 07000007.bin main map 47, names+flags 0x221/0x21/0x20], drawn from textures `002f:003e`/`002f:0055` (64×64, RGB
≈ black mean 3 sd 0, the shape in the ALPHA channel 0–255) as list-1 (flags & 1) batches with ALPHA_1 0x44 normal
blend, TEST_1 0x5001B (only A=0 discarded), ZBUF per leaf, vertex rgba ≈ (14,14,14,67) — i.e. subtle dark shadows
in the game. Measured headless (probe_render4): **the port has 0 untextured World groups, 0 out-of-range texture
REFs, 0 coronas (0xFC) and 0 searchlights (0xDE) on 07000007/07000008** — "missing texture" and "wrong object"
theories are dead; the port binds the same textures and per-pixel GS state the game's packets carry.

**What the decompile added [M]:** `psiCreateEntityGfx` 0x1171b0 resolves each texture REF addr through the 0x10
texture-header entry (+8 word → runtime record → record+0x1a u16 → global upload chain `DAT_00254ae8`), and
`psiCreateMapTextures` 0x11d200 dedups textures by pixel CRC into that global table — so the port's
`maps[map].textures[addr]` binding is pixel-equivalent even where the global id differs. `psiStartAlpha` 0x124900 /
`psiEndAlpha` 0x124920 only set/clear `AlphaFogObjects` (the list-1 distance fade, active only when `FogOn`) — the
port's fog=2 shader path already gates identically. `View_DrawObjList` 0x1e69a0 reads `bCharacterLight`
(obj+0xFE bit 2) and `bShadowCharacter` (bit 3) per object for the VU1 pipeline — the port ignores obj+0xFE
entirely, and those VU1 semantics are hand-written asm (untraced, gs-leaf.md "Not verified").

**Not fixed, and why.** No GPU here, so the port's on-screen colour for those decals can't be compared with the
user's screenshots; every headless check (texture content, blend/test/depth per batch, REF resolution, list
routing, corona/searchlight presence) matches the game. The two candidate deltas for the next pass (main agent has
the GPU): (a) the `bShadowCharacter` VU1 path — if set on these objects the game forces their output colour/alpha
in ways the port never models; (b) R2's depth rule — the game's 24-bit integer GEQUAL depth with coplanar decals
vs the port's f32 LessEqual (z-fighting shows decals through floors). What should change on screen: the pale
blue-white solid quads near stairs/railings must become faint dark soft-edged shadows on the floor.

**The 07000002 real-walk dump (dump_render4.rs) — the concrete port defect, not fixed this session.** Walking Bond
(teleported beside the bathhouse civilian at (−20,1,34), then at the plate positions) and dumping every drawn
drone with the requested fields shows: the bathhouse guards d00/d01/d03/d06/d07 (skins 0x05000036/3a/39, team 1,
ch 21/23) and the team-3 "captain" bodyguards d22/d23 (skin 0x05000034 "captain" [D], team 3, modes 7/5, dtypenew
14, ch 22/23) are **`started=false`, `enabled=true` at tick 0 and end in WAIT_SWITCH with `enabled=false`** — the
port's WAIT_SWITCH enter (drone.rs `(WAIT_SWITCH, ENTER)`) disables the drone, and the port's disabled drones are
not posed (no animation) and not hit-tested — while the renderer still draws their placement meshes (Scene::build
adds every char instance). The user therefore sees a frozen, unhittable guard standing next to the hostage. In the
game, WaitSwitch stops vision/AI engagement but the drone stays at its post with its idle pose and takes damage.
The teleport-walk over plates 341/383 (kind 0xEA → ch 21 [D]) did not raise ch21 headless — Bond got jammed at the
upper-floor plate positions, so the plate wake is still unverified end-to-end; the channel raise via the real
trigger path needs an unobstructed walk route. NOT FIXED.

**Not done this session** (each with its reason): G-041 bullet decals (small-medium, out of budget); G-042
skin-texel check (needs the civilian skin's texture identified on disc); O5 searchlight beam/corona (07000007/08
have 0 searchlights; the 07000006 beam work needs screen checks); the 07000005 torso flip and 07000006 stationary
guards (no new evidence; fix-drone3's clamp is still in); the searchlight→alarm music event (Searchlight_Update's
sound call not yet identified).

Determinism: no code changed, no RNG draws added. Files: the two new test files only.
## main-1: performance — collision ray bounds, GPU skinning, render interpolation (2026-10-11)

- **Sim (`NF_PROFILE=1`, new `nf_game::prof`):** 07000007's tick was 15.4 ms, 12 of it the per-drone `drawn` ray (`visible_to`): static collision had only per-object boxes and the party's rooms are single objects of thousands of triangles. Static geometry is now split into 16-triangle runs, grouped 32 at a time; segment queries slab-test both levels. Identical hits (full suite). Tick: 07000007 15.4 → 1.7 ms, 07000006 1.8 → 0.46 ms.
- **GPU skinning (G-043):** `Scene::frame_state` (the matrices `animate` built) and `colour_mults` were split out; `skin_layout` gives each Character-layer vertex two palette indices, a weight and a colour slot, and `skin_palette` builds one frame's matrices (per character: object + skin·object per bone; attachments, searchlight parts, doors, pickups) and colours. The vertex shader blends `w·P[a]p + (1−w)·P[b]p`. `gpu_skin_live.rs` proves it equals `animate`/`posed_vertices` on 05/06/07 (max error 1.5e-5, colours exact) with a sister test. Per-frame CPU: posed vertices ≈ 16 ms + 4.6 ms upload → palette 1.5 ms.
- **Render interpolation / high refresh:** logic stays fixed at 60 Hz; frames draw between the last two ticks (camera and palette lerp, snapping jumps > 4 units). Vsync at the display rate by default; `--fps N` caps with vsync off. `NF_NOINTERP` disables the blend.
- **Portal walk** (`fix-perf-level`) made opt-in (`NF_PORTAL=1`): it hid all of 07000006 between the truck and the courtyard.

## fix-cutscenes — the loadable cut-scene packs (`isLoadable` / `LoadableLoad`), the party Drake scene and the gondola intro

Area: the script players' streaming arm (`SP_LoadScript` 0x1dbc08 → `isLoadable` 0x1d69a0 → `LoadableLoad`
0x1d69e8 → `LoaderLoad` 0x1d4a00 case 0), the level-start path (`nf_view::load_with_carry`). Branch
`s/fix-cutscenes`. Playtest items: the 07000007 party cut-scene where Bond first sees Drake, and the
07000008 (gondola) cut-scene that should start almost immediately; plus the survey of every level-start and
intro cut-scene (docs/systems/levels.md §5).

**Root cause [M]:** the two cut-scenes' scripts are not in their level archives. Each level's type-0xC
entries register (script hash, flag) pairs (`LoaderProcess` 0x1d4880 case 0xC: u32 at +0, u8 flag at +4,
one record per entry), and `LoadableLoad(hash, flag)` builds the pack file name from the CURRENT LEVEL's id
with the (flag+7) nibble at bits 20-23: flag 1 → `078000NN.bin`, 2 → `079000NN.bin`, 3 → `07A000NN.bin`
[measured on the disc: 07000007's (0x06000072, 2)/(0x06000073, 1) → 07900007/07800007, which contain exactly
those kind-7 scripts plus their kind-4 sequences; the same holds for 01/02/08/09/0b/0d/11/13/14/16/1b/4a].
The port's script lib held only the level archive's kind-7 entries, so the mode-0 ScriptPlayers hit
`Player::load`'s missing-script arm (state 5, deleted) on their first trigger and the cut-scene never
played. The party chain: TouchOnce #356 (box 92.9–98.0, 49.0–53.8, −79.8–−78.9) → ch 0x15 → SP #419 plays
0x06000072 (the 3000-tick fly-through with the camera sweep and every guest animated — the Drake reveal);
TouchOnce #412 → ch 0x48 → SP #420 plays 0x06000073 (the control-taking scene, 3 × event 4/5/6/7). The
gondola chain: Bond spawns at (139.5, 50.5, −76.4), TouchOnce #237 ~3.5 m away → ch 0x49 → SP #294 plays
0x06000077 (3880 ticks) — "starts almost immediately".

**Reproduce before fix [NF_ISO, shown failing]:** `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_cutscenes_live.rs` — 3 symptom
tests drive the real path (`nf_view::load` → `step_bond` into the trigger triangles → ch → SP) and failed
before the fix ("SP deleted itself on its trigger — the pack script was missing"); the 4th (the 07000007
urn SP #312, mode 64, mask 2) is the priming control and passed.

**Fix:** `load_with_carry` reads the type-0xC records and merges each pack's kind-7 scripts into
`level.nis` (the lib `Scripts::new` reads) and its kind-4 sequences into the animation set — mirroring
`parsemap_parsemap` (LoaderProcess case 2 walks the entries). Two measured subtleties:
- **Pack sequences never join the level's per-skeleton list.** The game DELETES the animation hashtable
  before streaming a pack (`LoadableLoad`'s `hashtable_delete_hashtype(0x4000000)`) — the cut-scene's
  sequences replace the cache while it plays. The port's per-skeleton list is order-sensitive gameplay
  data (`frame_of`'s `k % len` idle cycle, the skeleton-filtered `seq_index` drone lookups): appending to
  it changed guard animations and broke 07000001's `dropped_guns_dim_to_the_cel_ambient` ("the guard
  died"). Pack sequences go under the sentinel skeleton key `0x80 | skeleton`, which still reaches the
  by-hash map (`Scene::seqs`) that `Script_AnimStart` resolution reads.
- **The level-start intros now play like the game's.** 07000001's SP #277 (mode 1, pack 07800001) and
  07000002's #400 (pack 07800002) play at load — verified against the game's own snapshot [L
  ee_start_07000001.bin: SP 0x18fbf70 = state 2, play 0x1, clock 42, length 2120, script 0x06000087].
  The intros fire event 4 (Bond disabled) and event 0xD (07000001: ch 0xB, which releases its waiters and
  brings an arrival in), so four test files (fix_player2/3_live, fix_ladder_live, render2_live's
  dropped_guns) now skip the intro the way the game lets the player (hold the skip action,
  `Scripts::skip_request` → `Script_FFwd`) before running their scenarios. Test-only adaptations for the
  corrected post-intro world: the raptor-drop take loop approaches each drop from the four cardinal
  offsets (a walking player takes a drop from the open side), drops whose column has no walkable floor at
  or above them are logged and exempted (the ch-0xB arrival's drop lands under the courtyard slope), and
  the crosshair sister tries the next enemy when the first is occluded.

**Survey (docs/systems/levels.md §5):** every cut-scene ScriptPlayer on the 20 story levels + the wrappers —
loadable-pack scenes (§5.1, all playable now), archive-resident mode-1 level-start scenes (§5.2, already
played), mode-64 preloads (§5.3), and the intros (§5.4): `ResetMap_Load` 0x1d6360 creates one ScriptPlayer
per level from the movie-code table only when the SUBTITLES option is on (`DAT_002a37c8`), and all 14
scripts in `07000500.bin` are single op-0x1E text streams — subtitle timings for the intro MOVIE, which the
port does not play (no PSS player). 07000005's #71 (0x06000074) has no loadable record and no pack on the
disc — the real game cannot stream it either.

**Not done (left):** `SP_Hit` proxy trigger bits (0x2 bullet / 8 / 0x10) — 07000007's urn break (mask 2,
primed) still waits on them; the `GameFlow_PushState(12.0, 0xD, 0xFF)` streaming loading screen; the C2-class
viewer dump on 07000002, the 07000005 torso-twist / 07000006 stationary-guard and searchlight-alarm items —
drone.rs/searchlight.rs are outside this task's file list. The pack's kind-4 sequence merge is eager (level
load) where the game streams lazily at first use — same content, no RNG-order impact; noted in
script-player.md.

**Verification:** the 3 symptom tests + priming control pass; full suite green on the slim ISO except the 3
allowed disc_golden failures (nf-formats 74 tests, nf-audio 7, nf-game 133, nf-view 106 — 0 failures).


## fix-ladder2 — the ladders draw, the climb look, the weapon save/restore, the crouch footsteps

Branch `s/fix-ladder2` (from origin/master 923595b). Tests: `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_ladder2_live.rs`
(NF_ISO) + the `climb_look_turns_within_the_ladder_window_and_pitch_is_free` unit test in player.rs.
Probe: `crates/nf-view/examples/probe_ladder2.rs` (weapon 0x47's record, the 07000002 water geometry,
the pool collision from above).

**1. The ladders weren't drawn — root-caused and fixed.** The ladder (placement 0x22) is a dynamic
object (`parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` 0x1d04f0 case 0x22 → `Ladder_Create` 0x1966c0); its
placements never carry the 0x8000 CREATE_CEL flag [M 0x1d1998 vs 0x1d1b68 — the static-cel path and
the dynamic-object path are mutually exclusive per placement], and `Scene::build` draws
`level.instances(cels_only=true)` — every placement without 0x8000 dropped. The game draws each ladder
exactly once through the generic dynamic-object path: `View_DrawObjList` 0x1e69a0 dispatches on
`obj+0xFA` (no ladder sets the anim/particle bits) → `View_DrawObjectGlist` 0x1e6780 renders
`obj+0xD8` (the celglist = the placement's resolved object, stored directly at 0x19671c, no
`Control_SetGList`) at `obj+0x90` — the placement transform `control_create_object` 0x1344e0 builds
(`View_RotTransMatrix` 0x1e5168); class 0x2D has no update function so `obj+0x90` is constant [M].
A straddling sphere reroutes to `View_AddForcedObjects` 0x1e5fb8 — still exactly once [M
Controls_StraddleTest 0x134778]. No ambient dim (obj+0xF0 stays 0; `View_SetupRenderModes_Tweak`
0x1e5888 white branch) [M]. Port fix (scene.rs): 0x22 retained out of the instance loop + a sweep
that instances each 0x22 placement's resolved object at the placement matrix, World layer, mult 1.0,
counted in the new `Scene::ladders_drawn`. Test: 07000002 draws exactly 4 (the disc count [D]), 07000005
exactly 1 [D]; the exact count doubles as the double-draw guard.

**2. The camera couldn't move on a ladder — fixed.** `Player_Climb` 0x196310's look: the turn channel
(`bd+0x34`) still integrates into the yaw after `Player_Climb` (`Player_Update`'s `bd+0x30..0x3F` →
`obj+0x50..0x5F` integration [M 0x193600]) inside the eased ±90° window (`diff = AngleDiff(yaw,
ladder.yaw+π)`, hard snap beyond ±π/2, ease `yaw += diff·0.2` with the PRE-clamp diff [M 0x196310:18-33]);
the ease pauses while the aim key is held — AnimObj bit 0 IS the aiming flag, cleared by
`Player_WeaponNone` on the grab [M 0x1a9858:18-19; the atlas's [S] upgraded]. The pitch offset
`BL+0x8A8` takes the stick freely during the climb (`Player_Aiming` runs for every substate ≤ 7 [M
0x1a1d28:21-30]; `Player_ViewClamping` clamps ±1.0 [M 0x1a92e8]). Port (player.rs climb_tick):
`yaw += input.turn` after the clamp+ease, `pitch += input.look` clamped ±1, ease gated on `!aiming`.
Note the equilibrium: a held turn settles at deviation = turn/0.2 (the ease opposes the channel) —
0.25 rad at the test's 0.05/tick; that IS the game's math.

**3. The weapon is now saved on the grab and re-equipped on the dismount; hands can't fire.**
`Player_WeaponNone` 0x1a9858 saves the current id to `anim+0x64` and goes to 'G' (0x47) immediately
(no holster cycle — `anim+0xF4 = 0`) [M]; the port ran a switch_request cycle instead and never saved.
The dismount carry `if (AnimObj+0x62 == 'G') AnimObj[99] = AnimObj[100]` [M 0x196310:99-102] plus
`Player_SetWeaponAnimObj`'s idle path re-running `Player_WeaponSelect` [M 0x1a2e38:197-201] is the
restore: the port now queues `switch_request = saved_weapon` on the dismount tick (scene.rs). The
'hands fire once' bug: weapon 0x47's record has NO fire scripts (+0xB0/+0xB4 = 0, no idle +0xA0
[D probe]) and the round spawn runs from the state-9 fire-script release path (`Player_SetFiringAnim`
0x1a3c70 → case 9 0x1a2e38:416-420; the press-tick spawn for +0x44 == 0 sits behind that call [M
0x1a5460:681-690]) — the port now blocks the trigger when the record carries no fire script. Fists
keeps its fire script 0x060006de [D] — punching unaffected. Tests: the grab saves 2 → hands, firing
at hands spawns no bullet, the dismount restores the P2K (all through `Sim::step_bond`).

**4. Crouch-walking "rapid footsteps on metal" — root-caused and fixed.** `AnimObjectUpdate`
0x1befd8:163-198 [M]: the stride is 1.65 EXCEPT while the CLIMB substate (1) runs — 0.4125 with the
fixed `Sound_Play3D(0x286)` at Bond (the rung sound); every other step is `Effect_Create(…, foot|0x42)`
→ the floor surface's footstep. The port had attached the 0.4125/0x286 pair to CROUCH. Fix (scene.rs):
the stride/sound special case keys on `substate == SS_CLIMB`; crouch steps run the normal 1.65 surface
path (the crouch anim's smaller per-tick displacement slows them naturally). The climb's step distance
is 3D (the game's `anim+0xD8` follows the anim up the rungs) [*suggested* — horizontal elsewhere].

**5. Swimming from a bank — repro recorded, NOT fixed.** [D probe_ladder2] 07000002's garden water
(cel 17): collision floor 3.7647 vs surface 3.7675 — Bond stands ON the water (pos.y − 0.3 ≫ surface,
`Player_InWater` 0x195e50 never fires); the deep pool (cel 16) has NO floor below the surface within
14 units, but the deck around it sits 0.5–1.0 ABOVE the surface, and every probed pool point hits a
floor at 4.23–4.74 from above. The port's `capsule_push` is double-sided (*Deviation*, world.rs —
"the game's triangles are one-sided by their stored plane; the port's winding is not known to match"),
so Bond stands on planes the game's player collision would let him fall through — the likely root
cause, but flipping sidedness needs the winding convention verified against the game's stored plane
data first (not done — no time). The repro lives as `#[ignore] swim_repro_walks_on_the_water_from_the_bank`
(asserts the CURRENT broken behaviour; flip it after the fix).

**Not done this session** (each with its reason):
- The vent grate / creepwall (07000002's vent): researched — there is NO grate class [M: all decomp
  "grate/vent" hits are Music_Event substrings]; the crawlable vent is a creepwall (placement 0x3F →
  `CreepWall_Create` 0x196fc8, class 0x2B; use → `Player_Activate` 0x1a5170's unarmed nearest-0x2B
  branch → `Player_CollCreepWall` 0x196758 → substate 7 `Player_Creep` 0x1969d0 with `Music_Event(0xD,1)`

- The level-select weapon fallback (`Player_InitWeapon` 0x1a7ef8): researched — `Player_EquipWeapon`
  0x1a8a58 refuses a weapon whose +0xDC FP skin is absent; `Player_CheckWeaponsLoaded` 0x1a97c8 zeroes

  give path lives outside my named files).
- The searchlight spotted→alarm MUSIC half on 07000006: researched — the chain is Searchlight_Update
  0x1cb900 (arm test: spot within 2.0 of Bond) → state 1 sets `ch[param3]` every tick →
  `DroneFunc_CheckAlarmRaised` 0x1453a8 counts `ch[0x37]` → `Music_Event(2,1)` → `UpdateMusicalEvents`

- C2 (scripted/ally drones drawn but not hittable/no AI), the 07000005 patrol torso twist, the grenade

## main-2: the muzzle-flash light, render side (2026-10-11)

- `Player_MuzzleFlash` 0x1a4298 → `Light_Create` (disasm 0x1a4370–0x1a43a8) [M]: radius = weapon_data+0x58,
  intensity 2.0, rgb = +0x56/+0x55/+0x54, life 0 (so `Light_Update` deletes it next tick: one tick per shot).
  Ported render-side: `Scene::dyn_light` → the shader's `lp`/`lc` uniform; `Vertex::nrm` carries normals (World
  rotated to world space, posed ones rotated by the palette in the shader).
- The shading is STANDIN: `lc × 0.25 × N·L × (1 − d²/r²)²`, tuned by eye; the VU1 formula is unread (fix-lighting).
- Failed first: keying the light on `last_shot == drones.frame`. The shot is stamped before the drone tick
  advances the frame, so the light was never on. The first "lit" 07000005 shot only showed the flash sprite,
  and its brightness gain was the sprite. Fixed with `Sim::shot_tick`, caught by `lighting_live`.
- Failed second: a zero normal fell back to N·L = 1, so the radar, the snow and the sprites lit full orange. Zero
  normals are now unlit.
- Not ported: the `Rand_Rand(0)` in `Light_Create` and the `Gas_Init` smoke `Rand_FRand` (sim RNG order), guard
  muzzle lights, level lights.

## fix-truck — the 07000005 truck park against the 05-truck trace

Branch s/fix-truck (from origin/master 5056ab4). Repro + fix tests: `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_truck_live.rs`;
the un-ignored harness: `crates/nf-view/tests/level_reload_live.rs::truck_ride_to_the_castle_ends_the_level`.

**The symptom** (reproduced headless first): `nf_view::load` + the viewer's `--bond 100,26,108` setup, tick 7000 —
Bond parks at (29.879, **38.376**, 51.971) vs the trace's (29.885, **37.887**, 51.656), and ch 0x70 (the truck's
parked-position TouchOnce plate, player-mask 0x8) never fires, so 0x65/0x1D/LOAD_LEVEL never run. The rest of the
chain was already live: the gatehouse cut-scene (SP #38, 0x060008C8 via ch 0x5C) disables Bond at t1884 and hands him
onto the truck at t2028, ch 0x71 is on for the whole ride, ch 0x22/0x72 fire on the way through the gatehouse.

**Root cause — the capsule height, not the truck's collision.** Measured through the port's own data path:
- The bed's only resting surfaces are part4 0x020003be's hull: bed-floor top 37.28 (visual mesh = collision mesh,
  same 36.248..39.496 AABB; block 0x2E), underbody 36.25, no surface at ~36.8 anywhere under the park spot [D].
- The game's standing pos-to-floor is 1.086 [L trace level start: obj+0x30 24.963 over floor 23.877 measured through
  the port] — the port's 1.096 matches it, so the convention is right.
- At the park the trace's pos−floor is **0.607** — 0.48 BELOW the standing offset, with no collision surface there:
  the game's Bond in the bed is not standing on the bed floor at the standing height. The game's capsule height is
  DYNAMIC: `obj+0xCC = obj+0x3C` every tick [M Player_Update 0x193600:449, Player_CollisionHandler 0x1949a8:182],
  the stance's root height above the feet; the anim/stance writes `obj+0x3C` (`Player_StandAtNewPosition` 0x190d88
  takes the placement vec4's W; `Player_Enable` 0x195498 copies the free script's matrix translation row — W
  included — onto obj+0x30..0x3C; `Script_Free` 0x1da880:45 passes SCRIPTINFO+0x40 and the +0xAB6 mode). The trace's
  ride is CROUCHED: park pos−floor 0.607 − the 0.051 standing rest offset ⇒ cc ≈ 0.556 ≈ the capsule radius [M
  0x194df0's 0x3f0ccccd]. The hand-off bounce in the trace (f33800–33900: y 19.7..20.95 ±0.6) is the stance
  transition; the port's fixed standing capsule ignored the stance entirely, so a crouched ride still parked at
  floor + 1.135 = 38.41 [shown failing: fix_truck_live on the pre-fix code parks 38.414].
- The ch 0x70 plate is a flat quad at y 37.7418 [D script stream 6 key 8], and the touch capsule runs from pos+0.15
  up with radius 0.55 [M Toucher::player] — the standing park misses it by 0.234; the crouched park reaches it.

**Fix** (crates/nf-game/src/player.rs, riding/capsule only): `Bond::cc` — the dynamic capsule height [M obj+0xCC =
obj+0x3C], standing `ROOT_HEIGHT` 1.0347183 [L], crouched `CROUCH_ROOT_HEIGHT` 0.55 [L trace-derived ≈ the radius,
tagged in the code]; `capsule()`, both floor rays and the grounded test read it; the crouch toggle swaps it
([S] simplification: the game's cc follows the anim pose per-tick, the port per-stance). Result: the crouched ride
parks Bond at 37.929 — 0.042 from the trace's 37.887 (the residual is the port's resting band, 0.099 vs the game's
0.051; the task's bar was ±0.05).

**Verified** [M tests, NF_ISO]: `truck_ride_parks_bond_at_the_game_height_and_ends_the_level` — park y ±0.05 of
37.887, x/z within 0.5 (the port parks at z 52.14 vs the game's 51.66 — the ride path's own slide), and the full
chain ORDER against the trace: 0x22 → 0x72 (rel −317) → 0x70+0x65 same tick (rel −300) → 0x73 (rel −273) → 0x1D →
level_exit 0x07000006. Fail-before: on the pre-fix player.rs the same test parks 38.414 and panics. Sister:

## 0090 — fix-hud: the HUD remainder (fire-mode/name labels, pickup messages, damage direction, air bar, crouch icon) + the language tables

Branch `s/fix-hud` from master 6faffb4. Task: port the missing HUD elements from the HUD_* decompile with
headless NF_ISO tests, per docs/systems/hud.md.

**Language tables (new, `nf_formats::hud::Lang`):** `Txt_LoadLanguage` 0x1caad0 loads `FNames[SelLang]` —
FNames[0] = "DUTxt.dat" is Dutch; the NTSC-U default read back from the disc is `USATxt.dat` [D FILES.BIN].
On-disc layout measured and verified: `u32 dataBytes`, data, pad of `4 - (dataBytes & 3)` (4 even when
aligned), `u32 NumEntries`, `u32 offsets[NumEntries-1]` (entry i ≥ 1 at `data[offsets[i-1]]`, entry 0 =
the heap sentinel), `u32 NumFixups`, `u32 fixups[NumFixups]`; `Txt_BindLabel` 0x1cad60 = `fixups[id>>24]
+ (id & 0xffffff)`. Read back: 0x200000D "Picked up %s", 0x200000E "Picked up %dx %s", 0x200000F "Picked
up Armor", 0x2000010 "Picked up Code Key", 0x200004A "007 Bonus collected", 0x2000051/52/53 the objective
strings. `nf_view::load` parses `USATxt.dat` into `Sim.lang`.

**Ported (crates/nf-view/src/hud.rs + Sim::hud_tick in scene.rs):** the ammo pane's fire-mode label
(`weapon+0x30 + mode*4`; the port has no fire-mode switching, so mode 0 → "Semi" for the PP7) and weapon
name (`weapon+0x38` → "Wolfram PP7") at (496, 432) layer 28, with the `BL+0x95E` 60-tick timer (set when
the HUD's weapon id changes and the records' +2 words differ, bright/dim 0xFF/0x1C swap per the decompile
— note: at rest the NAME is bright, during the timer the FIRE-MODE is bright [M 0x19a7f0:206-235]); the
pickup message bar (pane 21: `Text_AddMsg` 0x1b0c30 queue over `drones.taken`, 180 SP ticks, text fade
alpha = time·17 over the last 15, close 16 px/tick [M HUD_UpdateStatusPane 0x19c310], bar 256×26 at
(128,364) tex 0x0300007A, text centred (256,380) font 2 0x7D6D59); the damage-direction glow (BL+0x967
bits 1/2/4/8 → HealthSprInfo 20/21/22/23, tex 0x0300018D/0x0300018E with the table's flips, alpha
BL+0x968; `PlayerHealth::pain_from` ports the view-space rule of Player_DealWithObjHit 0x194458:201-226

## main-5: R2, the navy holes in the walls (2026-10-11)

- Found from the user's F12 screenshots (nf-shots 002/003/005 on 07000007) and reproduced headless at the logged
  spots. The navy was the clear colour: holes in the walls, not dark decals.
- **Cause:** the baked shadow decals (`hall_shadow*`, `banistershadows*`, the shadows behind the paintings) share
  the walls' list-0 draw state (pass 1, normal blend, zwrite, TEST 0x5001B). The front-to-back sort drew a decal,
  whose centre is nearer than the big wall's, BEFORE the wall it lies on. Its depth write, even where its alpha
  is near 0, rejected the wall. Which one won depended on the camera position, so it showed only up close.
- **Fix:** list-0 draws with an alpha-shaped texture (`gpu::alpha_shaped`: more than 1/4 of the texels below half
  the peak alpha) draw after the opaque ones of their pass. The game draws room cels before the objects on them
  (`View_DrawCelGlist` 0x1e6538, then `View_DrawObjList` 0x1e69a0) [M]; the texture test stands in for that
  split [S]. 249 of 4,811 list-0 World draws on 07000007 move.
- Rendered after: soft banister shadows on the stair wall, soft shadows behind the paintings; the 05 start view
  is unchanged. Test: `decal_order_live.rs`. Full suite: 354 passed.
- Also: `--bond` takes a 5th value (pitch), and F12 / the panel's screenshot logs it.

## fix-npcs — the C2 "drawn but never attacks / can't be damaged" class, the searchlight spot ray and the 07000006 alarm music

Branch `s/fix-npcs` (from origin/master 7e75c58). Playtest reference: docs/playtests/2026-10-11.md (C1/C2/C3,
the 07000005 torso item, the 07000006 searchlight item, the 07000007 guest retest). Tests: `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_npcs_live.rs`;
the regression fix in `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_drone3_live.rs` (shared test file, minimal, noted below).

**The diagnosis that reframes C2.** The bathhouse/end-of-level "drawn frozen guard" is the port's ch-waiter drone in
`NDrone2_DSTATE_WaitSwitch` — and in the GAME that drone is an INVISIBLE statue: WaitSwitch ENTER calls
`NDrone2_Enable(0)` [M 0x15b960:14-17] which sets `obj+0xF0 |= 0x10|0x20` (View_AddObjects 0x1e62d8:33 drops 0x10
objects from the draw; Collide_PickObj 0x1eae80:26-30 drops 0x20 objects from the pick) and clears `+0x4F8 & 0x1801A0`
(no anim/AI) [M 0x149dd0:8-15]. It wakes only when its live switch channel fires [M 0x15b960:21-37]. The earlier
fix-render4 WORKLOG claim ("in the game, WaitSwitch stops vision/AI engagement but the drone stays at its post with
its idle pose and takes damage") is WRONG — corrected here; the decompile and the [L] waiters (`obj+0xFC = 0`, hit
sphere 0) both say invisible-and-unhittable. On current master the port ALREADY hides the post-intro waiters
(state 1, enabled false, the renderer's hidden gate at scene.rs) — the user's playtest predates that gate. Verified
headless on 07000002 at tick 3000 (post-intro): d00/d01/d03/d06 in WaitSwitch, enabled=false, `frame_state.hidden=1`;
the civilian woman (d21, team 2, HostageIdle) enabled and drawn. `dump_drone4`'s dump "doesn't match play" because
its whole observation window (~542 ticks) sits INSIDE the level-start NIS freeze (~1540 ticks), where nothing has
started yet — that is why fix-drone2/4 could not reproduce the symptom headless.

**What was actually broken and is fixed — the NIS-freeze window.** During ANY cut-scene the port left every drone
per-drone `enabled=true`: the renderer drew them frozen (the user's symptom class on 07000005's gatehouse scene and
every intro), and a bullet already in flight could still hit and damage them. The game: `Drone_EnableAll(0)` walks the
whole llist calling `NDrone2_Enable(0)` per drone [M 0x1383e8:13-23], `Drone_CollisionHandler` returns while
`NPCGlobals == 0` [M 0x140968:62], and `Script_Free`'s 0x80 flag re-enables every drone EXCEPT state-1 WaitSwitch ones
[M 0x1da880:41-43, 0x1383e8:14]. Port fix (drone.rs): `Request::DroneEnable` now mirrors per drone
(`enabled = on && state != WAIT_SWITCH` for present drones), and `update_player_bullets`' drone-pick loop is gated on
`npc_enabled`. Fail-before: `fix_npcs_live::the_intro_freeze_disables_every_drone_and_shields_them_from_bullets` on
07000002 at tick 120 (mid-freeze) — pre-fix all present drones `enabled=true` and a fired bullet damages the nearest;
post-fix all disabled and the bullet passes through. After the intro the waiters sit in WaitSwitch disabled and the
civilian stays enabled+drawn (asserted).

**The 07000006 stationary guards (C2 there) — the same class, plus a working-AI lock.** Post-intro dump: 20 of 25
guards are ch-waiters (channels 11/12/13/15/16/18/19/55) in WaitSwitch disabled — invisible statues the game wakes by
trigger; d14/d17 sit on always-on channel 185; d02/d15/d16/d14 are enabled IDLE guards. The enabled idle guards
behave: `an_idle_gate_guard_sees_and_attacks_bond_on_the_same_floor` walks Bond in front of d15 — los within 70 ticks,
alert 1.0, into the combat chain, Bond takes damage to 57. (The IDLE enter sets `+0x4F8 |= 0x10000` [M 0x15bf18:30] —
the port's vision_on — and Idle UPDATE's `EnemyLookForOpponent` returns 0x56 [M 0x177ed0]; both already ported by
fix-drone3.) The waiters' wake path stays fix-drone3's ch-55 test.

**The searchlight spot ray picks the player [M], ported.** `Searchlight_Update`'s spot ray runs with pick flags 0x18,
and Collide_PickObj's mask mapping excludes the player's class ONLY under mask 0x400 [M 0x1eae80:26-40] — the ray hits
Bond's world sphere (`obj+0x80`, r `obj+0x8C` = 1.0576 [L]) when the beam is on him, which is what makes the arm test
`Vec_Dist3D(spot, player) ≤ 2.0` [M 0x1cb900:251] fire at shallow angles where a static-only ray runs past him. The
port's ray tested static geometry only (the main agent's diagnosis; fix_drone3_live's teleport-onto-the-spot test
passed while play failed). Fix (searchlight.rs): ray-vs-sphere on top of the static segment; the closer hit wins, the
spot orients by that normal. Fail-before shown with a pinned synthetic head over the real 07000006 world
(`the_spot_ray_picks_bond_and_arms_the_light_from_his_sphere`): pre-fix the spot never draws and the light never arms;
post-fix the spot lands on Bond's sphere (dist 1.31) and the light arms (state 0→1) and raises ch 55. (The test
geometry needed the open sky at y 150: the castle's room-boundary planes at every z and the covered courtyards leave
no un-occluded chest-height ray on foot — measured by probe and recorded here.)
**The first cut of the fix had a real bug the regression suite caught**: `spherical(100, …)` returns a 100-length
vector and the ray-sphere quadratic assumed a unit direction — the spot flew to −10000 and fix_drone3_live's
searchlight test failed. Fixed (a = |dir|² in the quadratic); the incident is kept in this log because it is exactly
why the full suite runs before every push.

**The 07000006 alarm music — the missing dispatch, ported.** The chain up to `Music_Event(2,1)` was ported
(fix-drone3/ladder2); `UpdateMusicalEvents`' per-level dispatch ran `UpdateMFX_01CastleA` for 07000005 only
[M 0x114e70 → 0x113060]. `UpdateMFX_01CastleB` is `under_attack ? PickRandomCombat(0) : PickRandomStealth()` [M
0x113060:26-30] — ported as the 0x0700_0006 arm of the dispatch (nf-game/src/music.rs). The NIS-trigger half
(DAT_002d3524 == 0x6000071 → the MapMusicData+0x14/+0x18 marker jump) is NOT ported: the MapMusic parse lacks those
marker fields (a separate nf-formats change, left to the audio session). Test: `Music::the_07000006_alarm_demands_combat_music` (nf-game/src/music.rs) streams
`Music_Event(2,1)` per frame — the combat jump lands on the 12th tick (the hysteresis's alert_frames), targets the
combat set; sister: a quiet 07000006 picks nothing. Shown failing pre-change? The dispatch arm is new code — the
fail-before is the behaviour itself (pre-fix no `UpdateMFX` ran for 0x0700_0006 at all, so no jump could ever issue;
the pinned-head searchlight test's ch55 half plus this unit test pin the two halves of the chain).

**The 07000007 guest retest — already fixed on master, verified.** fix-drone4's `a_party_guest_walks_her_mission_route`
passes with the freeze mirror in; the routed guest walks, PartyGirls stand (game-accurate [M 0x160140 case 3]), the
waiter guests stay disabled. `the_party_waiter_guests_stay_disabled_and_the_walkers_settle` locks the post-intro
state (no enabled guest in a combat state). The guest walk is a one-shot mission route (arrived clears prop 0x1D →
Civilian), which is why the user sees stillness after the first walk.

**The 07000005 patrol torso item — verified, no code.** fix-drone3's two-sided ±0.9 clamp is in and its test passes;
a re-read of `AnimObjectAimAt` 0x1bfe58 confirms the port's sign convention is self-consistent (the game's aim angle
comes from `acos` + the scalar-triple-product sign, not a yaw difference, so there is no absolute left/right datum to
copy) — the "spine flipped" report matches the pre-fix-drone3 build. Remaining known gap (not ported, G-026 family):
head tracking (`AnimObjectHeadTrack` bone 5, max dist 3.0, rate ~0.13 [M 0x1472c8]) — cosmetic, left to a render-side
session.

**Shared-file notes.** `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_drone3_live.rs`: the searchlight chase capped at +3 over Bond's
start feet — with the player-pick sphere the spot rides his sphere once the beam is on him, and the old uncapped
`spot + 0.4` chase walked him into the sky. `crates/nf-game/src/drone.rs` and `searchlight.rs`/`music.rs` are this
task's named files; scene.rs untouched (the existing hidden gate already keys on the per-drone `enabled` the freeze
now clears).

Determinism: no new RNG draws on the shared path (the freeze mirror and the bullet gate add none; the test's
`fire_player` call consumes the sim RNG exactly as a real shot does); the fixed 60 Hz tick path unchanged.
## 0091 — fix-wire: the cable crossing (Player_CollWire + Player_Wire + Player_Zipline)

The user's report: at the cable left of the castle gate (07000005), pressing E plays the falling-to-death
animation instead of the hand-over-hand crossing. Root cause: the port had NO wire gameplay at all — the
old `wire.rs` derived endpoints from "translation + glist extent" with misnamed params (`channel` = param 2,
`glist` = param 3), and the only wire code was a proximity hack that posted `Music_Event(0xD, 1)` when Bond
walked within 1.5 units of a wire (scene.rs `creeping`). Walking at the cable did nothing; the spot is over
the chasm, so Bond fell (tests/wire_repro.rs: substate stayed 0, y 33.37 → 32.18 in 30 ticks).

What was ported (crates/nf-game/src/wire.rs, crates/nf-game/src/player.rs, minimal scene.rs/dev.rs plumbing):

- `Wire` rebuilt from the atlas: instance bytes = params 1/0/2/3 at inst+0x00/02/04/06 (type, param0,
  param2, switch channel — the old field names were shifted); endpoints derive at grab/ride time from the
  world sphere (centre + radius from the placement's object bounds through the yaw-only matrix — the live
  07000005 sphere centre/radius match the snapshot [L ee_start_05 016dc430]); grab segment radius − 2.0 at
  obj+0x58 pitch [M CollWire 0x1971f8], travel radius − 0.5 pitch 0 [M Player_Wire 0x1976f8], zipline full
  radius at pitch [M Player_Zipline 0x197ff0]. `Wire::all` resolves placements against their map objects
  like `ladder::all` (the hardcoded 4.0 length is gone).
- Segment direction pinned by disassembly: `Vec_Spherical_2_Cartesian` 0x1e3948 computes
  (r·sin θ·cos p, r·sin p, r·cos θ·cos p) of the yaw ARG (its internal `+π/2` builds the cos), and the wire
  call sites add π/2 to obj+0x54 before the call [M 0x1971f8]. With 07000005's yaw −1.5708 the wire runs
  along Z — the atlas's "endpoints ≈ (−19.95…−27.03, …)" X-span used a cos/sin-swapped reading; corrected
  in the atlas.
- `Player_CollWire` 0x197130: the grab guards (regrab, type ≠ 1, substate ≠ target, zipline lower-end
  refusal), ClearInertia, substate 6/0xF by type, mode 0xC + anim 0x060005e5 (type 0) / 0x06000095 (type 2),
  hang offsets 1.0207 / 1.17363, the yaw = the nearer of wire.yaw ± π/2, the hand-reach correction from the
  grab anim's root delta (x − 0.082, rotated — signs reconstructed from the MMI disasm [S]), cam mode 0xB.
- `Player_Wire` 0x197658 (substate 6) whole: the travel-segment endpoint snap (SqDist2D), the auto-drop
  timer (+100/(60·30) per tick, paused in the grab pose, drop past 100), the drop path (jump press →
  saved_sub, cam 0, regrab 0x1E, AnimObj[99]=[100] via the Sim's re-equip carry), the strafe-axis move
  modes 7/8 with the end-zeroing band (within 0.5² of the travelled-to end or past the far one), the idle
  pair 0x060005ec/ed, the turn pair 0x060005ee/ea and the move pair 0x060000b4/b5 with the decompile's
  oldhash alternation and the ±0.0542 sway (perpendicular to the facing), the per-add clamp onto the line
  at closest.y − 1.0207, and the anim root motion (the tracks sampled from the level archive's kind-5
  scripts + the anim archive's sequences; the move pair travels 0.7637/0.7106 per cycle at the ±1.2 rate
  [D measured]). No fall check while attached [M — the decompile has none].

## fix-player4: fists knock out (the punch hit path, the KO state machine, the punch alternation)

The task's three evidence lines (fix-player3, WORKLOG item 7): the punch is a bullet with 1.75 range, the KO state
is at 0x172a30, and the port did 5.0 damage with no knock-out. All three now ported.

**Who sends a drone to KO on a weapon-1 hit** (the pass fix-player3 could not fit in): `NDrone2_DealWithObjHit`
case 5 (0x13fff0:269-306) — the shooter is the player, so the WEAPON picks the message: 1 (fists), 0x4B, 0x4D →
**msg 6 (punch)**; 0x4A/0x4C → msg 7 (taser); 0x43/0x44 → msg 0x19; everything else `Drone_BulletHit` msg 8. The
state table at 0x29b300 [L ee_start_05.bin] maps **0x42 → NDrone2_DSTATE_KnockedOut_Anim** (0x172a30), 0x43 →
Knocked_Out (0x172b48), 0x53 → PunchImpact (0x172ee0). `DroneFunc_HandleImpact` case 6 (0x1469b8:34-57) calls
`NDrone2_PunchImpact` (0x145f28) with the state's resume/allow — and a scan of all 250 DSTATE decomps shows msg 6's
(resume, allow) equals msg 8's in every one of the 46 states that carry a case 6, so the port reuses its msg-8
table. `PunchImpact` stamps the resume into +0x118, applies the damage through `DoHitEffects` → `HitDamage` (a head
punch reads as a torso, 0x145558:25-30), and at health ≤ 0 enters **0x42** (mode 0x1E bots → 0xF2, not ported);
alive it staggers (anim 0x51 → +0x118, both flinch stamps) when allow, else enters the resume state — the (0x56, 0)
pairs are what turn a punched idle guard hostile at once.

**The KO state machine** (0x172a30, disasm-checked): ENTER — corpse flag 0x20, alert status 3, health = 0,
`CallAnim(0, 0x50, 0, next 0x47)` (the fall), `+0x4F8 |= 0x1000000` (the KO flag), `DroneWeap_DropWeapon` (the
one-visible-gun drop at KO time), `PlrStat_LogEnemyDisabled` for enemies. EXIT — `SetDeathChannel` on every level
EXCEPT {0x07000009, 0x0700000A}: the guard at 0x172b14 is `sltiu` (UNSIGNED), so 07000005's difference 0xfffffffc
passes. Cases 8/9 → Death_Anim 0x44. There is NO OnInitDeath in the path: no death talk, no grenade drop. The KO
flag makes `OnInitDeath` (0x145bd0:22,57-59) and `NDrone2_LogDroneDeath` (0x14ab00) skip
`PlrStat_LogEnemyDispatched` — **a KO'd guard counts as disabled, not killed**, and never gets back up (the fall
anim ends in Dead 0x47 → Fade 0x48 like any death).

**The punch alternation**: `Player_SetFiringAnim` (0x1a3c70) — flag 0x80000 weapons (the fists, +0x68 = 0x880A2 [L
record 1]) draw `Rand(100)` per shot and play +0xB4 (0x060006DD) on > 50, else +0xB0 (0x060006DE): the left/right
punch, one shared-RNG draw per punch. Flag 0x1000/base-0x11 last-round and the 0x40000 strict toggle (+0x958) are in
the same function; the port's `Gun::firing_anim_script` ports all of it and `scene.rs` calls it.

Port: `drone.rs` — msg::PUNCH (6), states 0x42/0x43/0x53, anims 0x50/0x51, `update_player_bullets`' weapon→msg
route, `on_punch`/`on_impact`/`on_punch_resume`/`punch_impact`, `handle_knockout` (ENTER/EXIT/update + 0x43 + 0x53),
the KO observables (`knocked_out`, `disabled_logged`, `dispatched_logged` — the dispatched log sits where
OnInitDeath runs, DEATH_ANIM/SpecialDeath enter). `gun.rs` — `alt_fire_toggle` (BLData+0x958) +
`firing_anim_script`. `scene.rs` — one call (the fire-script pick; shared file, ~10 lines).

Tests: `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_player4_live.rs`, driven through `nf_view::load` + `Sim::step_bond`:
`punching_a_guard_knocks_him_out_without_killing` (pre-fix: "the punch KILLED the guard (state 0x44)"; post-fix: 2
punches → 0x53 stagger → 0x42, no 0x44 in the state log, health 0, disabled not dispatched, the one-visible-gun
drop; sister: a P2K shot guard logs dispatched, not disabled) and `the_punch_fire_script_alternates_left_and_right`
(10 punches in the air; every pick predicted from a clone of the shared RNG taken before the press; both scripts
play, 5/5 on the level seed). Full suite in the commit.

## fix-mission: the mission layer — objectives, mission flow, level ends, the 07000001 escort exit

**The system** (docs/systems/mission.md is the API contract for the parallel tasks): `MissionData`
(0x2a4350) + the 24 named objective tables decoded — the 0x18-byte objective record is +0x00 text label,
+0x04 fail label, +0x08 hint label, +0x0C condition channel, +0x0D init value, +0x0F enable channel,
+0x10 flags (bit 1 = the channel ON fails), +0x14 runtime state [L ee_start_05.bin; the readers
0x1827d8/0x182270/0x182630; U-024 closed in docs/formats/mission-data.md]. The port embeds the tables as
`mission::LEVELS` (`crates/nf-game/src/mission/c0<level>.rs`, texts resolved from USATxt.dat).

`Mission_Init` (0x182270, from `ResetMap_GameInit` 0x1d5080:53), `Mission_MonitorObjectives` (0x1827d8:
the per-objective state machine 0→3/2→4/5, the AND over every part of the mission → success ch 100, the
0x60 "Killed Civilians" / 0x61 "Alarm Raised" fail hooks) and `Mission_Update` (0x182c60: ch 99 →
"Mission Fail" → the 0x40000042 menu — the port restarts the level; ch 0x62 (player dead,
`Player_HandleDeath` 0x190bb0:32) → the death flow; ch 100 → "Mission Complete" →
`ResetMap_LevelToLoad(LevelToEndTo)` — 0x0730xxxx driving levels logged and skipped) — all ported in
`crates/nf-game/src/mission.rs` (a new module), hooked at the end of `Drones::tick` (shared file, ~12
lines: the mission fields, the lazy init, the tick, the ch 0x62 death write).

**The HUD** (nf-view/src/hud.rs + scene.rs): the objective banner (pane 3: 480×56 at (16,0), the status
label 0x02000051 "NEW OBJECTIVE" / 0x02000053 "OBJECTIVE COMPLETE" at (128,20), the text at (128,40),
left-aligned per fmt 0x30cdb0, alpha time·17, close 16 px/tick) and the mission banner (pane 2: 512×103
at (0,156), "Mission Complete"/"Mission Fail" centred at (256,42), the FailLabel line at (256,64)
flashing 0x785A14 while a type-2 notice is up, close 32 px/tick) [M 0x19c310; the SprInfo tables L
0x319580/0x319608]. All strings resolve through the existing `Lang::bind` — the mission label ids are
bank-2/4 (0x02000053…), NOT the 0x20000053 nibble order a first pass guessed (the tests caught it).

**The 07000001 exit end to end**: the level-start intro's event 0xD writes ch 0xB [L ee_start_07000001],
releasing Mayhew (skin 0x0500004F, mode 12). The real gap: mode 12's start state 0x1c is
**AllyLeadInit** (`NDrone2_StateFuncs[0x1c]` [L 0x29b300]; `DroneTypeSettings[12].start` [L 0x29aee8]) —
the port had 0x1c mapped to a standing HostageIdle, so Mayhew never walked. Ported AllyLeadInit/Lead/
Wait/Done (0x15e4f0/0x15e698/0x15eda8/0x15f2e8) over the port's existing mission-route machinery
(`update_mission_route` = `UpdateMissionRoute` 0x154a80); the flee/combat sub-states (0x1e/0x1f/0x21/
0x22/0x28) and `ObjectMissionPathDistance`'s exact wait rules are stand-ins for 038-fix-actors. The
end-to-end test: the intro plays unskipped → ch 0xB → Mayhew leads ~199 units along path 0 (kind 8) →
Bond E-opens the courtyard slide door en route → Mayhew reaches the plate (AllyLeadDone) → Bond joins →
Touch #137 (out 0x10, filters [player, skin 0x4F]) → LOAD_LEVEL → `level_exit = Some(0x07000002)`.

**Tests** (`crates/nf-view/tests/fix_mission_live.rs`, all through `nf_view::load` + `Sim::step_bond`,
each shown failing pre-fix): the objective lifecycle (07000005's enable 0x45 → "Breach the castle walls"
→ condition 0x46 → OBJECTIVE COMPLETE; sister: an unrelated channel does nothing), the alarm fail
(07000009: the alarm button's channel 0x7C → the disc's own OR (placement 278, out 0x61) → "Fail: …" +
FailLabel "Alarm Raised" + ch 99 → "Mission Fail" → the restart; sister: no alarm, no fail), mission
success (every part's channel on 07000001 → ch 100 → "Mission Complete" → LevelToEndTo 0x07000048; the
AND is unsatisfied one channel short), and the end-to-end escort exit. Docs: docs/systems/mission.md
(new, the API), docs/systems/levels.md §7 (all 55 objectives per level), docs/formats/mission-data.md
(U-024 closed).
## map-tower2 — the second tower missions 07000011–07000014 mapped, walkthrough-tested and made completable

Branch `s/map-tower2` (origin/master d91f5bd + the fix-mission mission layer cherry-picked — the task's
"build on mission.rs" instruction; the WORKLOG merge conflict resolved keeping both entries). Playtest
reference: docs/playtests/2026-10-11.md. Docs: docs/levels/07000011.md … 07000014.md (new). Tests:
`crates/nf-view/tests/walk_070000{11,12,13,14}_live.rs` + `walk_tower2_probe.rs` (the live state probe and
the kind-5 script scanner), all driven through `nf_view::load(_with_carry)` + `Sim::step_bond`.

**The mission chain.** Mission 0x07000011 = 07000011 → 07000012 → **0700004A** (part 2, the lobby connector
[L c0700004a.rs]) → 07000013; the objectives' channels fire one level late by design ("Gain access to lower
office floor" 0x48 ← TouchOnce #679 on 07000012; "Escape through the elevator shaft" 0x4D ← TouchOnce #277 on
0700004A; "Gain access to lobby" 0x4A ← TouchOnce #153 on 07000013) [D, every writer hunted per level and the
misses documented]. Mission 0x07000014 = 07000014 alone (5 objectives, ch 0x47/0x48/0x4A/0x54/0xCE), ending in
07000015.

**Fix 1 — the mission globals ride the RamSave** (walkthrough 07000013 failed pre-fix: "Gain access to
lobby" never completed). The game keeps `MissionState`/`BaseMap`/`ThisOrderNum`/`FailLabel` and the
per-objective states in `.data` across `ResetMap_LevelToLoad` — `Mission_Init` 0x182270 only resets the
current and future parts in place [M 0x182270:68-129]. The port re-creates `Mission` per load, so previous
parts' states reset to the `.data` defaults and the success AND could never see them. `RamSave` now carries a
`MissionSave` (the LS_MakeMission/LS_LoadMission 0x1cd720/0x1cd880 payload shape) and `Drones` restores it
after the `Mission_Init` latch [M]. Shared files: player.rs (+field +builder), drone.rs (+field +3 lines),
lib.rs (+2 lines).

**Fix 2 — the fuseboxes** (walkthrough 07000014 failed pre-fix: the sabotage chain 0x87+0x88 → AND #391 →
0x8C had no writer). `FuseBox_Create` 0x1b0448 (0x31 + script hash; params 1–4 = the two wire groups'
channel words), `FuseBox_Register` 0x1b0970, `FuseBox_Update` 0x1adfe8 ported in `fusebox.rs` (new): the
group scan, both channel words written when a group empties, and the **live-wire 5.0 hurt** through the same
`Player_Hurt` → `pain_generic` path the explosions use [M 0x1adfe8 `Player_Hurt(0x40a00000)`]. Stand-in,
noted: the wires are one abstract wire per group cut with E after the lid press (`Player_Activate` 0x1a5170
reaches the box's class-0 SP first); the SP-entity bullet path is not ported. The level's five boxes are
mapped in docs/levels/07000014.md §5 (the completion path needs #383 + #385).

**Fix 3 — the SimpleScript open/closed swap** (the driver's named 07000012 item). The disc evidence: every
animated 0xE2 pair member's key 0 equals its placement transform, and the pairs are complementary — at rest
the closed/covering member sits in place while the open/parked member rests away; the trigger channel
(p3 — 0x58 shutters/screens, 0x59 lift) runs each member to its other key [D, the level's 0x19 blocks 12–20
decoded key by key]. `SS_Create` 0x1a9c58 creates an object only when the record's key count
(`extra[7] & 0xffff`) is non-zero; `SS_Update` 0x1a9948 poses it every frame via `KeyFrame_Interp` 0x1e1140.
Ported as `ss.rs` (new): key 0 at rest, the playhead runs toward the last key while the channel is on and
back while off (rate = `extra[7] >> 16`, 0 → the default 75). The animated 0xE2s left the static scene pass
(level.rs, 3 lines) and draw posed through the door slot space in scene.rs (the vertices index
`door_base + n_doors + k`; the upload fills the region from `drones.sss.list`). The E-call-buttons #699/#702
(out 0x58/0x59) drive the swap; verified by `walk_07000012_live::the_lift_call_button_swaps_the_simple_scripts`
(the leaf at x 2.206 → 3.070 [D block 15]). The key-less 0xE2s keep the old static draw (the game creates
nothing for them [S — the barrel-trap note]). simplescript_live's assertion follows the posed pass.

**The walkthroughs** (each level doc carries the full chain):
- 07000011: the cold start at #146 → the spawn touch 0x7E → the stairwell down → E at the Load Point #158 →
  07000012. The atrium fall is the scripted death (the y-42 plates #314–318 → SP #313 → 0x0600098A event 0xD
  [0x62,1] → the restart) — already ported, now pinned by a test.
- 07000012: the spawn touch completes 07000011's objective (the late AND); the override console #731 (E, out
  0x49; the E arm has no lock read — [M 0x1b2318], the test documents the lock's real polarity); the shaft
  touch #683 holds 0x1F → the gated exit #669 → 0700004A.
- 07000013: the warm chain arrives with 0x48/0x49/0x4D on; the spawn fires 0x4A; the front entrance (#156 →
  0x50, then the ch-0x64 touches) completes the mission → `LevelToEndTo` 0x07300013; the gate exit #72
  requests the driving interlude on E (ch 0x4E has no writer — dead auto-fire data [D]).
- 07000014: the five stages (vent 0x47 → Kiko 0x48 → the sabotage 0x8C → the room escape 0x4A → Rook 0x54 →
  the exit 0xCE + 07000015), the exit's key gate locked until Rook falls (the sister test).

**Full suite**: green except the 3 allowed `disc_golden` failures on the slim ISO.

## map-mayhew — the Mayhew estate missions 07000005-08 mapped, the objective layer ported, walkthrough tests

Branch `s/map-mayhew` (from origin/master 6a012ee). Docs: `docs/levels/07000005.md` … `07000008.md`. Code:
`crates/nf-game/src/mission.rs` (new file, this task's own), one additive hook in drone.rs (`Drones::mission` +
the tick monitor), the volume-containment branch in triggers.rs' `touched_by` (shared file, noted). Tests:
`crates/nf-view/tests/walk_0700000{5,6,7,8}_live.rs`.

**The objective layer [M Mission_MonitorObjectives 0x1827d8, Mission_Update 0x182c60] — ported in mission.rs.**
The game's table is 18 records of 0x28 bytes at EE 0x2a4354 ([L] ee_start_05.bin, dumped: every record's level
field = the mission's FIRST level code — the Mayhew records all read 0x07000005), each objective { label, fail
ptr, +0x0C complete channel, +0x0F reveal channel, +0x10 flags (bit 1 inverted), +0x14 state }. The monitor per
tick: state 1 + reveal ch → 3; state 3 + complete ch → 4; inverted objectives fail (ch 99) when their channel
turns on; the all-done AND is LIVE over every objective's channel condition; ch 0x61/0x60 → fail (ch 99); all on →
**ch 100** + Music_Event(8,1). `Mission_Update`: ch 99 → fail (end 0x7000048); ch 100 → complete → `LevelToEndTo`
per level — **0x07000008 → 0x07300008 (the DRIVING hand-off)** [M 0x182c60:85-116]. The port runs the whole table
(18 records — the other map sessions build on it) against `base_map(level)` (the chain ranges [S, pinned by the
table's base codes and the driving switch]). The Mayhew chain [L]: 0x4000000 "Breach the castle walls" (ch 0x70,
reveal 0x45) → 0x4000001 "Find a way inside to the party" (ch 0x02, reveal 0x70) → 0x4000002 (ch 0x48, reveal
0x47) + 0x4000003 (ch 0x49, reveal 0x48) → 0x4000004 (ch 0x4A, reveal 0x49) + 0x4000005 (ch 0x4B, reveal 0x4A).
Not ported (the HUD/fail screens): Text_AddMsg presentation, MenuManager_Create, the unarmed-impact fail reasons
(SetMissionFailReason 7/2/0xb — the reason plumbing is 031-fix-mission's file).

**The LoadPoint containment fix [M Trigger_Hit 0x1b1fc8 does NO geometry]** — it classifies the object's CONTACT
LIST (obj+0xD0), which the collision pass fills for anything overlapping the trigger's glist bounds. The port's
triangle-only `touched_by` missed a toucher standing INSIDE a room-shaped volume (07000006's LoadPoint #746: 6
tris forming an open box [D measured] — a capsule inside touches nothing). `touched_by` now also hits when the
toucher capsule is fully contained in the trigger's bounds. fail-before: walk_07000006's dress step (ch 0x83
never pulsed pre-fix, the dressing scene never started).

## fix-lighting — the dynamic lights: the VU1 point-light formula, the sim-side light list, the muzzle light + guards' + level lights

Branch `s/fix-lighting` (origin/master 9aac84e). Task: the user's PCSX2 comparison — lights fall on
characters and firing lights the surroundings; the port only applied the flat cel ambient. Playtest
reference: docs/playtests/2026-10-11.md (the lighting items live under Rendering).

**The VU1 microcode, read at last (G-014).** ACTION.ELF `.vutext` (0x241c80, 0x2880 bytes = 1296
instructions) + the six `.DVP.overlay` sections disassembled with a purpose-built decoder (field
positions and opcode tables cross-checked against PCSX2's DisVUops.h/DisVUmicro.h; the pairs are
little-endian qwords = {lower, upper}; lower opcode 0x40 = the special table; the tool lives in
~/dl/vutext/vudis.py, not committed). Findings:
- The base image is a DVP monitor: a jump table at I-mem 2..25 (MSCAL entries 0/2/4/6...), a
  dispatcher that reads the packet's own slots (`ILW +20/+22(VI2)`, VI2 = 2) and `JR`s into
  overlay code; `BAL VI15` links; the packet lives at VU1 data address 0.
- The light setup (I-mem 595-608, reached from the dispatcher) loads packet qwords 0-7 = the matrix
  chain, **8/9 = the two light positions** (FillMatrixChainRot 0x122310 transformed them into the
  object's rotation space), **12/13 = TColor0/1** (rgb·intensity·tint, **w = 1/radius²**,
  `psiLight_SetLights` 0x10e588), **15 = TAmbient** (= the object's TWEAK: `psiSetTweakARGB`
  0x124770 stores 0x2650d0; `sceVu0LightColorMatrix` 0x229108 packs rows TColor0/1/2/TAmbient at
  packet 12-15).
- The point-light program (I-mem ~832-940, one software-pipelined iteration per vertex): L =
  lightpos − pos (object space, `SUB`); d² = |L|² (componentwise `MUL` + the ACC broadcast-sum with
  fs = VF9, whose y = `ADDw.y VF9, VF0, VF0` = **VF0.w = 1.0** — the VU's VF00 = (0,0,0,1) [M PCSX2
  vuMemReset], which also explains `MULAw ACC, VF4, VF0` = the matrix's W row and `DIV Q, VF0.w,
  d²` = **1/d²**); atten = `max(0, 1/d² − 1/r²)` (`SUBw VF24, VF28, TColor.w` then `MAXx.xy`);
  diffuse = `max(0, atten · dot(N, L))` with the **RAW unnormalised L** (componentwise `MUL` +
  broadcast-sum; no RSQRT in the program); the sum `TAmbient ⊙ rgba + TColor.rgb · diffuse` (895
  `MUL VF22, VF12, VF28`, 911/912 `MADDAx/MADDy`); the normal enters as the packed stream int ×
  1/128 (`MULi VF26, VF29, I`, I = 0x3c000000 from the LOI). Both atten and the product clamp at 0.
  The second colour matrix (packet 16-19, `LQ.xyw`, rows from PS2Viewer+0x120.. /256) is the
  directional/cel matrix path (View_DrawCelGlist's `flags & 4` twinkle) — not ported.
- The selection sort: `QuickSort(SortList, n, 4, 1, 0)` uses the comparator at 0x1d3350 — ascending
  by `light+0x38` = `d/(radius·0.5)`; accepted kinds: 0 needs obj-flags 0x80, 1 skips 0x100, 2
  needs 0x80 with the 2D (xz, `Vec_Dist2D` 0x1e2ec8) distance ≤ 4.0 and intensity
  `(1 − d·0.25)·50` [M 0x1cb40c], else 3D ≤ sphere + radius; max 30 entries.

**New `crates/nf-game/src/light.rs`**: the `light_tag` record (0x50-byte layout: pos +0x10, life
+0x20, channel +0x22, flicker +0x24..+0x2C, track +0x30, falloff +0x38, radius +0x3C, intensity
+0x40, rgb +0x44..46, kind +0x47, active +0x48), `LightList` (the pool grows, no fixed cap [M
Light_Create mallocs 0xa00 = 32 × 0x50 when the free list empties]), `Light_Create` with the
unconditional `Rand_Rand(param_11)` draw (state advance is argument-independent; the 10-arg call
sites leave param_11 uninitialised for the counter seed — [S] the flicker path re-derives it),
`Light_Update` (life countdown + delete, the channel gate, the flicker state machine; the flicker's
`Sound_Play3D` not ported — the placement calls leave the sound id uninitialised), the selection
(`resolve` → `ResolvedLights::closest/pick2`, one implementation for the sim tests and the
renderer), and `shade_vertex` (the VU1 formula above, world space — the game's object space is a
rigid transform of it, N·L invariant).

**Wiring** (all [M] with the address in the comment):
- Drones owns `pub lights`; `Game_Run` 0x1c9790:33 runs `Light_Update` before the object movement,
  so the update sits at the top of `Sim::step_bond` (the port's drones.tick runs after the fire
  path and deleted the fresh muzzle light same-tick — caught by `lighting_live`).
- Bond's shot: `Player_MuzzleFlash` 0x1a4298 → `Light_Create(radius = weapon_data+0x58, 2.0, the
  muzzle, rgb +0x56/+0x55/+0x54, life 0 → +0x20 = 1, kind 1)`, gated on weapon_data+0xDC ≠ 0 &&
  +0x48 ≠ 0; then `Gas_Init`'s `Rand_FRand(2π)` unless +0x68 & 0x2000 (the smoke puff record is
  sim-side [S] rise+fade; not rendered). The sim's muzzle position = eye + aim·0.5 [S] (the game
  uses AnimGetBoneWorldTrans datum 0; the render could refine it later).
- Guards: `DroneWeap_FireWeapon` 0x178f68:189 → `Light_Create(7.0, 1.0, the muzzle, the weapon rgb,
  kind 1)` between the accuracy roll and the bullet's spread draws — the port's `fire_weapon` does
  exactly that (the light list threaded through `handle_firing`).
- Level lights: block 0x26 (new `LevelMap::radiators`, 8 floats per entry [M
  `Light_SetAmbientRadiators` 0x1caeb8: x,y,z,radius²,pad,r,g,b 0-1], kind 0, intensity 1.0,
  permanent, one `Rand_Rand(0)` draw each) created before the placement walk; the type-0x4E
  placements (`parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` 0x1d04f0 case 0x4e: radius = +0x2C, rgb bytes
  +0x30/34/38, channel +0x3C, flicker +0x40, kind 0, permanent) created inside `level_drones`'
  placement walk so their draws interleave with the drones' creates.
- Searchlights: `Searchlight_Create` 0x1cb4f8:150-172 builds the kind-2 record inline (white,
  radius 500, intensity 1.0, tracked to the part) — one `Light` per kind-2 part with
  `track = part index`, resolved per frame against the part's live position (below the world until
  the first lock, exactly like the game); the kill path deactivates it.
- The renderer: the uniform grew to per-draw 256-byte dynamic-offset slots (vp + fog + lp0/lp1 +
  lc0/lc1); per draw, `pick2` on the draw's bounding sphere (`Material::centre/radius` — the game's
  obj+0x80 sphere) selects the ≤2 closest; sky draws select none. The per-draw flags gate passes
  0x80 for world/character/effect ([S] the port has no per-object obj+0xF0; emitters — the game's
  0x100 — don't exist as draws). The shader replaces the STANDIN `lc × 0.25 × N·L × (1−d²/r²)²`
  with the microcode's formula (colour at /128 for the port's 0x80 = 1.0 vertex scale; zero normals
  stay unlit). `Scene::dyn_light` (the render-only STANDIN path) is replaced by
  `Scene::frame_lights` → `Renderer::lights`.

**Tests** — `crates/nf-game/tests/light_selection.rs` (9, all fail on master: the module is new):
the falloff/radius gate, the kind gates with the kind-2 intensity, the ≤2-sorted-by-falloff upload,
life/delete, the create's RNG advance at arg 0, the record fill, the searchlight's tracked
position, the VU1 formula's exact values (atten 0 at d = r, 0.75 at d = r/2, backface clamp, zero
normal), and the render-independent sister pair — a character next to the muzzle light brightens
that frame, the same vertex without the light does not.
`crates/nf-view/tests/lighting_live.rs` (NF_ISO, rewritten): the muzzle light's weapon values,
one-tick lifetime, the frame view resolution, the shared-RNG advance, the smoke puff + the no-shot
sister.

**Failed first**: the kind-3 radius gate compared against r² (inv_r2.recip()) not r; pick2 fed the
falloff (not the raw 2D distance) into the kind-2 intensity — both caught by the new unit tests and
fixed. The muzzle light dying same-tick (Light_Update inside drones.tick running after the fire
path) was caught by `lighting_live` and fixed by moving the update to Game_Run's slot.

**Not ported** (each with its reason):
- The directional/cel matrix path (packet 16-19): the cel twinkle/rim uses PS2Viewer values — out
  of this task's scope, the world cels keep their baked colours plus the point lights.
- The smoke puff's render (the record + RNG draws are in; the game's `gases_smoke` particle render
  needs a billboard path the port lacks) and its exact velocity integration [S] model in place.
- The flicker's `Sound_Play3D` (the placement calls leave the sound id uninitialised).
- `Lights_CalcAmbientLight`'s per-character ambient bytes (obj+0x100) beyond what fix-render
  already applies; the character flags gating (0x80/0x100) is approximated per draw [S].
- The `TweakRGBA` +2 microcode entry (the TWEAK-colour program variant).

**Verification follow-up (same session):** the WGSL is parse- and validate-tested offline with naga
(`shader_tests::the_shaders_parse_and_validate` — the sandbox has no GPU adapter, so the shader had
never compiled here). Full suite after the re-baselines: 430 passed, only the 3 slim-ISO
`disc_golden` failures (the task's allowance). The report is `docs/reports/fix-lighting.md`.

## fix-levels-sweep — the 27-level headless health check (2026-01)

`s/fix-levels-sweep`. `crates/nf-view/tests/levels_sweep_live.rs` runs every on-foot archive in
FILES.BIN (27 on this ISO; driving 07000023-29 and the packs 07000500/07000999 excluded, 0e/f/10
absent from the disc) through the real Sim path: the smoke (load + 600 idle ticks, the required
NF_ISO test) and the deep sweep (1800 ticks of a scripted walk along the nav graph with E pressed
every half second, then one CPU pose pass — the GPU-less `--shot` counts only). Results in
docs/systems/levels.md §7.

Findings:
- **No panics on any level** (both passes assert). No unresolved objects, no pickups without a
  model anywhere.
- Unhandled placement types per level, each with its `parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` (0x1d04f0)
  creator: 0x21 Ripples, 0x26 MP object, 0x35 PCQWorm (lands with s/map-tower), 0x38/0x39 space
  laser/missile, 0x3a Grapple, 0x3b DynamicObject, 0x3f CreepWall, 0x41 InverterTrigger, 0x4a
  Apocalypse, 0x4e Light, 0xd2 Shooter, 0xd4 Cloud, 0xd5 OneSided, 0xd8 RB (rigid bodies), 0xda
  Car, 0xe3 Flicker, 0xe7 ThirdCam, 0xf2 Emitter, 0xf3 EnvTree, 0xf4 MoviePlayer, 0xfc Corona.
  0x17/0x23 have no case in 0x1d04f0 at all (map-block data).
- Unported drone state ids (no constant in the port's 88-state machine): 0x85 (mode 7 — the
  WORKLOG B-3d "stuck" stand-in) on 07000011/12/13/15, 0xa7 on 07000004, 0xb4 on 07000007 — the
  pass-through start-state ids from `DroneTypeSettings` with no handler arm.
- 0700001b: 11 of 74 ScriptPlayers still waiting on their gate channel (param 9) and 11 drones
  never enabled after 1800 ticks (`NDrone2_Enable` 0x149dd0 / the k15 wait-switch — the fix-npcs
  C2 class; no writer fired in the blind walk).
- The objective-channel writer scan (cross-mission: the monitor matches BaseMap, so sibling
  levels' writers count) closed two of the brief's known gaps:
  - **07000005's ch 0x46** ("Breach the castle walls") is written by **07000006's OR mux #498**
    [D: type 0xC out 0x46 list [0x32, 0x33, 0x34]]; enable ch 0x45 by 07000005's TOUCH_ONCE #36
    [D]. The record byte at +0x0E is NOT the init value — `Mission_Init` reads init from **+0x0D**
    [M 0x182270:118-124: `switch_channels[+0xc] = +0xd`], which is 0 for this record; the task
    brief's `46 00 01 45` reading put the init one byte late. fix-mission's records are correct.
  - **07000002/03's key-gate exit channels 0x4C/0x52**: both written (0x4C by an AND mux on 02
    [D trigger(out 3)], 0x52 by a script event on 03 [D script 0x06000082 event0d]).
  - The scan's param reader had to be **little-endian** — the port's `nis.rs run()` rd is LE
    (validated: `47 00 00 00` = ch 0x47, the map-tower2 doc's [D decode] agrees); my first BE
    pass reported garbage channel ids.
- Remaining writer gaps (levels.md §7.3): 07000008 ch 0x4B (the cable-car ride SP chain —
  `SP_Update` 0x1dbda8's out-hold does not raise it), 07000003 ch 0x4E (the Dragon Safe — the
  0x3b DynamicObject family, unported), 07000016 ch 0x90 (map-finale's scope), 0700000a/0b's
  Q-Worm channels (written by s/map-tower's PCQWorm, unmerged at scan time).

Full suite: 82 test binaries ok; the only failures are the 3 permitted slim-ISO `disc_golden`.
No product-code changes were needed — the sweep found no crash (the task's fix budget went to
the writer analysis and the tables).
## fix-pickups-trace — the Raptor drops match the real game's 01-raptor trace; the dev infinite-ammo refill no longer refuses every later drop

**Repro first** (`crates/nf-view/tests/fix_pickups_trace_live.rs`, NF_ISO, real path `nf_view::load` +
`Sim::step_bond`; shown failing by stashing the dev.rs fix — panic "drop 7 (weapon 0xe) is taken —
the user's symptom", with `NF_PICKUPLOG=1` showing `[take] weapon 0xe kind 0 rounds 6 → None` every
tick after the first take landed):

- **The user's bug**: with the play cheats (god + infinite ammo — the trace session's setup) the
  first Raptor drop equips but every later drop refuses forever. Cause [M dev.rs after_tick]: the
  dev refill wrote `carried[i] = max(carried[i], 200)` — above every ammo cap (type 3 caps at 36
  [D ammo_data]) — so `Player_EquipAmmo`'s cap check (0x1a8d18, ported in pickup.rs) refused every
  owned-weapon drop; and it topped **unowned** clips to their clip size, so the first take's
  `Player_EquipWeapon` (0x1a8a58) saw `old = clip[0xE] = 9` and pushed the whole drop's rounds into
  the spare instead of none.
- **The game's cheat shape** (what the trace session actually ran): the recorder tool
  (tools/trace/trace_record.py --ammo / cheats.py) tops each **owned** weapon's clip (BL+0x1B8+w·0xC)
  and each spare type (BL+0x170+a·2) back to the **most seen this run**, every 30 frames, resetting
  on a BLData change. Spares never exceed a take → no cap refuses (trace spare type 3: 0→6→13→20→25
  vs cap 36, every drop taken); an unowned gun's clip stays 0 → the first take adds no spare (trace:
  no type-3 event at 6.0 s).

**Fix** (crates/nf-view/src/dev.rs, `Dev::after_tick`): the infinite-ammo branch now ports the
recorder's cheat exactly — every 30th tick (`sim.drones.frame % 30`), owned weapons' clips and all
spare types topped to `best_*` (max-seen, only moves up), tables reset when `Sim::level` changes
(the tool's BLData-change reset); the `carried.max(200)` line is gone. God's armour write corrected
100.0 → 50.0 (cheats.py `F50`; the trace's armour column reads 50.0 throughout). Fields
`best_level/best_clip/best_spare` are pub (tests build `Dev` literals).

weapon 0x0E = "Raptor Magnum" [D USATxt label 0x0500002D], base 0x0E, ammo type 3, clip 9,
