## guard-reaction-delay — guards don't fire the instant they see you (started 2026-10-16)
Playtest: "guards shoot way too soon upon spotting you, at least give it half a second", "his gun's firing before it lowers at me" (07000006 wine cellar, searchlights, 07000005). Porting the game's sight-to-fire pipeline: noticed/alert latch timers, the aim-raise animation gate, the first-shot delay / reaction time (per difficulty if scaled), the searchlight-spot path. Branch s/guard-reaction-delay.

### guard-reaction-delay progress (2026-10-16 ~07:50 UTC)

- Verified the pending CombatNoRoute change against the decomp: [M 0x164c08:29-30] case 1 (ENTER) fires
  `DroneWeap_Fire(1)` and then clears `+0x3b` on the same tick (the entry tick cannot release a bullet);
  [M 0x164c08:41] case 3 not-seen clears `+0x3b` before ChooseCombatMove; [M 0x164c08:63] case 3 seen only
  refreshes `+0x3b = (+0x1e == 0)` — no NextBulletTime (no writer of Drone+0x1e exists in the decompiles, so the
  byte is 0 and the refresh is always 1). [M 0x17a8c0:9-14] DroneWeap_Fire gates NextBulletTime on `+0x3b` already
  set in SP (`MPSettings._388_4_ == 0`) — the port's `fire()` guard matches.
- New test crates/nf-game/tests/guard_reaction_live.rs measures the three sighting paths (07000005, the ai_live
  notice spot, positions only):
  - path1 fresh idle: sight ack 60 (live 61), ATTACK 60, first combat move 0x74 StepAimRight, first bullet 161.
  - path2 alert-1.0 (alarm-raised): self-attacks during the warm-up (AlertSound 0x177800 forced-attack bits, no
    sighting needed), sight ack tick 1 — the 59-tick floor is gone; first bullet 114 (a 100-frame step was in
    flight when Bond appeared).
  - path3 mid-combat re-sight: re-sight → COMBAT_NEW_SIGHTING → AimStandFire in 0-2 ticks (the entry fire
    0x166328:59-61); at dist ≤ 4.0 CanBackoff routes AimBackoff first (0x166328:96-102), so no bullet until the
    backoff ends.
- KEY finding (anim call completion): a class-3 danim call (the step/strafe moves) never completes in the port —
  guards sat in StepAimRight forever. The game's chain [M 0x13add0/0x13aee8]: when the transition danim of the
  call's state starts, `+0x57b` (reached) is set and `ZeroAnimCall` clears the request record but the completion
  action (+0x596 next AI state / +0x598 msg) SURVIVES; class 3 skips CallFullyComplete, so the call completes only
  when the step's FOLLOW-ON danim (class 2) starts after the anim ends — reached is still set and the follow-on's
  class 2 triggers `CallFullyComplete` → SetEndAIState(+0x596=0x68). The port's `call_handler` gate
  `matches!(class, 2|9) || (class == 1 && !once)` blocks class 3 forever, and the step danim here is a 100-frame
  one-shot (hash 100664390, anim set 5), so the guard steps the full 1.67 s, cannot fire during it
  ([M 0x1676a0:16-18] the step enter clears `+0x3b`, no Fire in the step update, and steps do not abort on sight),
  then AimStandFire releases. The port already mirrors this end-to-end (set_danim keeps the call + reached);
  the 100-frame step play-out is game-exact behavior, not a stall — the earlier "stuck in 0x74" trace was the
  test's 120-tick window, not a bug.

- The take query decoded to the end (fix-safe08b's open item, all ACTION.ELF): `Pickup_Update`
  0x18e148:213-214 → `Collide_LineOfSight` 0x1edf50(from = the player's world-sphere centre, to =
  the pickup's, cel = the player's obj+0x20, exclude = the pickup obj, 0, 0x721); the wrapper's
  disassembly (0x1edf50-0x1edf98) forwards `char = 0` — so `Collide_RayIntersect` 0x1ec690 tests
  EVERY candidate node (dynamic-owned included) — query word `0x721|4 = 0x725` (HITTEST+0x98) and
  mask 0x10 (HITTEST+0x9A), which arms the per-triangle `Collide_Filter` 0x1ed888 inside
  `Intersect_RayGeom` 0x10a8c8 (same 0xd/0xe rule as `Collide_Intersect`'s tail). `Collide_PickObj`
  0x1eae80 keeps a dynamic object unless obj+0xF0 & (0x20 | 0x1000) or its class byte (+0xff) is
  0x02/0x03/0x05/0x11/0x12; the SS door's class is 0x25 [M SS_Create 0x1a9c58:52] and the safe's
  shells carry glist flags 0 [D the level's records] — every blocker of the safe-room take rays is
  tested by the game too. A surface-6 hit survives every filter: the doorway take at the
  body-sphere facings that graze the safe's own shell refuses in the game exactly like the port
  (the origin is the yaw-rotated body sphere [L M_CONTROL+0x80]); the player collects by walking
  in. No take-path change needed — the port matches the query.
- THE FIX (a real one): the script-entity drain's fresh-push arm skipped `Pickup_Create`'s
  level-conditional rounds override [M 0x18dda0:116-118, applied inside the create so every arm
  gets it] — 07000008's SafePickUps rocket (the script word says 5 [D 0x060009E2 s1]) held 5
  rounds, so the take credited a phantom carried round (the clip is 4). Now
  `create_rounds_override(d.level, sp.id, sp.rounds)` in `drone.rs`'s drain; the reserved-slot
  path already applied it at reservation build (scene.rs `script_pickup_reservations`).

  nf-game/nf-view/nf-formats/nf-net classified by what its iteration order feeds. Tick entity
  lists are all Vecs; the shared Rng (drone.rs:387, seeded 0x1234_5678 in Scene::build) sees only
  deterministic code. Six order-dependent sites fixed: physics.rs `Tuning::get` (HashMap prefix
  tie-break → BTreeMap + (len,key)), scene.rs `by_hash` + `seqs` (skeleton-bucket last-wins over
  HashMap order → ascending skeleton id), scene.rs `view_model_chars` (values() order → build-loop
  order), weapon_assets.rs foreign-skins merge (HashMap order → ascending hashcode),
  nf-net session.rs desync-compare order (→ ascending tick). The rest verified lookup-only or
  order-insensitive (list in the report).
- THE GUARD (task step 3): `crates/nf-view/tests/cross_process_determinism.rs` + the child runner
  `crates/nf-view/src/bin/nf-cpd-child.rs` (via CARGO_BIN_EXE_, no libtest in the child). 600-tick
  07000005 combat (Bond parked in a live guard's sight, NewSighting gate, real fire/cover draws)
  fingerprinted per tick with mp::hash::Hasher (FNV-1a 64 over IEEE bits; frame → rng → bond →
  drones → bullets → grenades → explosions). GREEN: two full sim builds — bit-identical for all
  600 ticks (two builds ⇒ every std HashMap re-seeded ⇒ different iteration orders); the trip
  sister — a 64-entry toy HashMap folded into a separate column diverges from tick 91
  (4e3009c91fe1cc63 vs 27e7d6277a72cab3) while the state column stays bit-identical. The
  two-process leg (child runner, NF_OUT file) SKIPs with evidence in this sandbox (see below) and
  runs the honest cross-process comparison where process semantics are honest.
- SANDBOX QUIRK (cost the bulk of the session, documented): a libtest parent's spawned
  grandchildren misbehave here — Command::output()/status() return while the child still runs
  (captured stdout ends mid-load), the child's own file creations stay invisible to the live
  parent (they appear after the tool call), and the child's stderr only reaches the parent's
  original stdio. A plain parent (shell or a standalone Rust spawner: spawn + file stdio + poll)
  runs the same child perfectly in ~2 s. The child keeps both channels (NF_OUT file + stderr TICK
  stream) so the cross-process leg works on honest machines.

## searchlight-flip-06 (2026-10-16, work entry)
- `Mat_Align2Dir` 0x1df2a8 to the game's exact math [M disasm, tools/crosscheck/mipsdis.py]:
  (a) the degenerate cross ZEROES the row — the == 0 arms store 0.0 to all three components
  (0x1df2d8-0x1df310 / 0x1df3a8-0x1df3e0: `sqrt.s` then `c.2.s` against 0, the taken arm
  `swc1 f3(=0.0)` to the vector's slots) — the port's [1,0,0]/[0,1,0] stand-ins asserted world
  axes where the game's own math keeps the (exact-FP) cross direction sound — the only
  port-vs-game divergence in the basis; (b) the fallback threshold is 0x3f7fbe77 (0.998993 —
  `lui at,3f7f; ori at,at,be77` at 0x1df320-0x1df32c), not 0.999; (c) normalization multiplies
  by the reciprocal (`div.s f0,1.0,len` at 0x1df2f4/0x1df3c4 then the VMUL), it does not divide.
  The zero-dir shuffle arm also lands on zeros (the sum of squares is 0 only when every component
  is 0). The beam call's arguments were verified at the instruction level: up = fallback =
  Bond − head [M Searchlight_Update 0x1cb900 disasm 0x1cc020 `daddu a3,a2,zero`] — the port
  already matched.
- Tests (nf-view, real path `nf_view::load("07000006.bin")` + `Sim::step_bond`):
  every_06_beam_basis_stays_continuous_over_the_sweep — Bond parked inside head #2's sweep for
  1800 ticks (the boot NIS lights the heads, the sweep passes over him, the spot arms the tracker,
  the tracking leg included); beam_basis_stays_continuous_while_bond_walks_the_courtyard — the
  walking-Bond arm/track/lose cycle; a_straight_down_beam_uses_the_games_fallback — the sister:
  a real fallback gives the straight-down beam the cross(fallback, row2) basis [[1,0,0],[0,0,1]],
  the beam's own parallel-up arguments zero the rows, and a near-parallel cross normalizes to its
  own sound direction (never a world axis). The tick-to-tick assert compares only same-state
  active tick pairs (active_run ≥ 3): the light-up tick builds the beam from the stale state-3
  angles and the next tick's first sweep jumps — the game's own case-3 fall-through does exactly
  that [M 0x1cb900], so it is not a sweep flip (the first repro pairs were create→first-update
  and turn-on→first-sweep).
- The nf-view flip file 3/3; nf-game --lib 240/240 (the align2dir_matches_the_live_beam [L] pin

- ROOT CAUSE (rocket-glass-08, 21:45 UTC): the flight ray's first hit down the 08
  start corridor is the far window's pane at 19.62 u from the spawn — surface byte
  0x10 (glass), no 0x40/0x80, node pass clear [probe on the port's own loader = disc
  data]; behind it the plain wall (0x0a) at 22.87 u. The port's HITDATA walk
  (`flush_world_impacts` → `penetration_roll`) only knew the node/0x40/0x80 pass
  bits, so the rocket stopped on the pane. The game's handler has a GLASS RULE the
  port lacked [M Bullet_CollisionHandler 0x12ce80 disasm 0x12cf44..0x12cf64]:
  `if (!(weapon_data+0x6c & 0x800) && (HITDATA+0x50 & 0x3f) == 0x10) pass = 1` —
  material 0x10 lets any bullet through, no draw; the gate word is the WEAPON
  record's +0x6c (the disasm's `*(s0+0x44)` object — +2 is the weapon type word
  0x50/0x51 = the Q-Claw, +0x70 the explode/effects flags), so the Laser 0x4E
  (+0x6c = 0x900 [L]) burns the pane while the unguided 0x2d (0x1a200 [L]) passes.
  The pane-pass also precedes the Q-Claw type-word check in the game's order.
  Fix: the rule added to `penetration_roll(_node)` (new `flags6c` param, callers
  pass their weapon's +0x6c: drone.rs flush walk + the drone-bullet walk), no RNG
  drawn, stream unchanged. Effect: the rocket pierces the pane the tick it crosses
  it, flies on ~10 ticks and explodes on the wall face — the port's blast moved
  19.62 → 22.9 u, matching the PS2's ~24 u / ~72 frames within the task's ±1.
  Pinned rocket_glass08_live (3 tests: the unit glass rule incl. the laser gate +
  no-draw; the 08 start shot explodes past the pane at z −100.0, 21.9–24.4 u; the

## ladder-underwater-02 (task 750a)

The 07000002 underwater-ladder softlock (the user's third report). Root causes found and fixed on
s/ladder-underwater-02: (1) the climb substate's collision pass ran the fat 0.55 stance capsule —
the game's climb arm is r 0.275, A = up·0.55, B = up·(0.275 − cc) [M Player_Collision 0x194df0
case 0; the capsule switch indexes on substate−1 — disasm 0x19506c-0x195098 — so case 0 IS the
climb] — the 0.55 capsule wedged in the undergarden shaft above the deep ladder (−50.35, 5.50
[D]) and head_bump ate the up-push every tick: Bond hung on the ladder forever; (2) the swim grab
pick ran the CROUCH arm (the same mis-index: 0x194df0's "case 3" is substate 4, not the swim 3) —
the swim rides the switch's DEFAULT arm [M 0x195070 default] — fixed in ladder_grab; (3) the
neutral-settle re-latch after the bottom dismount is GAME-FAITHFUL: the settle at 0.5 off the
plane is inside the game's pick (mesh probe: the real glist triangles reach the settle capsule at
seg-tri distance 0.19–0.22 < 0.55), resolving 691's live check 1 — the escape is the push-off /
the climb-out, both now alive. Tests: crates/nf-view/tests/ladder_underwater_02_live.rs (5 tests,
real input path: the disc ladder/water census, the hut full-bank escape, the deep swim-in climb
out of the water, the deep climb-down + mid-water push-off clearing the grab column). Remaining

## frag-throw-timing (741)

- Symptom (playtest 1016-1355, 07000014): frag grenades leave the hand before the throw animation
  finishes — the port spawns them too early. Goal: the game's release frame for the frag throw
  (the fire script's spawn frame / the release-frame family [M Player_WeaponFiring 0x1a5460,
  +0x44]) and a fix that spawns the grenade on exactly that tick, measured from the press.
- Started: reading the decompile.
- The release path audited end to end [M]: `Player_WeaponFiring` 0x1a5460 tail — the fire tick
  queues the fire script, and for the `+0x6C & 0x400` + `+0xB4` family (the hand grenades
  [L ee_start_05.bin 0x34: +0x6C 0x8c08, +0xB4 0x0600049e]) stores view state 0xb and the script
  rate 1.5 (`AnimList+0x98 = 0x3fc00000`, disasm 0x1a6250 area); case 9's release check
  (0x1a2e38:411-422) never runs for the family — the state leaves 9 inside the fire tick. Case 0xb
  (0x1a2e38:499-507) waits `AnimScriptIsStopped` (the ended bit `+0x78 & 0x10000000`, set by
  `AnimScriptEnd` 0x1c1930:30) then queues the +0xB4 script; case 0xc (0x1a2e38:505-519, disasm
  0x1a3268-0x1a32c4) carries the release check `+0x44 <= AnimList(4)+0x90` — the +0xB4 playhead,
  which starts at 1.0 [M AnimScriptInit 0x1c1600:37] and advances 1.0/tick [M AnimScriptTick
  0x1c2630 mode 0].
- Frag facts [L ee_start_05.bin record 0x34 / the port's script parse]: +0x44 = 26, fire
  0x0600049d = 70 frames (pin sound 0x1e4 at frame 16), fire_last 0x0600049e = 35 frames. Release
  = 46 ticks of fire script at 1.5× + 25 ticks of the +0xB4 = press+71. The port released at
  press+17 (the case-9 check on the fire script's playhead-26 crossing) — the repro test measured
  exactly 17 before the fix.
- Bisect: fix-player2 eb1564b7 introduced the release check against the FIRE script's playhead
  (release +25 at 1.0×; the playtest 1014-1725 "released while I'm still pulling the pin");
  f986a6b3 (the 1.5× throw-cadence commit, Oct 15) moved the same wrong-gate check to +17 — the
  playtest 1016-1355 "way too soon, opposite direction". grenade-rattle2 (693b) touched the
  bounce-speed cap, not the release. The root error in both: the check ran during the fire script;
  the game's check for this family lives in the post-script state 0xc against the +0xB4 playhead.
- Fix: scene.rs's release block gates the family on `view_script == +0xB4` (the case-0xc phase)
  before running `release_frame_reached`. Test: frag_throw_timing_live (press+71, not the
  playhead-26 crossing, the fire script still playing at tick ≤20, one grenade per press, the
  record speed); the sister pins the fire script uninterrupted past the old crossing.
- The three tests that pinned the old gate (fix_grenade_release_live's release + launch-position,
  remote_mine_detonate's release frame) contradicted the decompile — fixed per the task rule, with
  the addresses in the assertions: the release is the +0xB4 playhead reaching +0x44 (case 0xc
  [M 0x1a2e38:505-519]), the frag at press+71, the mine (fire 40 frames at 1.5× = 26 ticks) at
  press+51. All four grenade-family test files green on the fixed tree.
